issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
EvalDash pins every scored view to one cohort and defaults it to `eval-policy-2026-09-24-verified` (#9461, #9752). The runs of the current eval policy (#10197, 2026-10-16) were launched with `experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/launch-campaign.sh` without `--version`, so their records carry `version: null`. The cohort dropdown lists only the verified policies plus non-null labels (`metrics.py`, `versions`), so these runs are reachable only through "Newest per benchmark (all cohorts)", and that mode disables Compare (`/compare` answers 400 "Choose one cohort before comparing models.").

Effects:

- Links shared before the cohort was written into the URL now open on the 09-24 cohort and show no scores. From the identity SFT thread (#10695): https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/compare?models=open-athena-Marin-Snowball-67B-A2B-v0.1,open-athena-Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A13-2026.10.30,open-athena-Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A3-2026.10.30 and https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/models/open-athena-Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A13-2026.10.30 . Every such link lands on an empty view until the reader picks "all runs" or the unversioned cohort by hand on the model page. Only the `runs?model=` links still work, because the Runs view spans cohorts.
- The default is an old policy. There is no verified cohort for the 2026-10-16 policy, so nothing launched today can land in a verified cohort, and the dashboard asks every visitor to pick a cohort before showing current results.
- Models cannot be compared across cohorts, and unlabeled runs cannot be compared at all.

Reproduce:

1. Open the compare link above. The page appends `?cohort=eval-policy-2026-09-24-verified` and lists no models.
2. On the Panel, choose "Newest per benchmark (all cohorts)". The models appear with scores; the compare checkboxes are disabled.
3. Look for a cohort entry for runs with a null version. There is none.

Expected: the links above open on the three models' current-policy scores and comparison. Current-policy runs belong to a selectable, comparable cohort. The default cohort is the current policy, or there is no forced default.

Done when:

- Records with `version: null` can be selected and compared through the cohort selector, `/panel` and `/compare`.
- The default cohort reflects the 2026-10-16 policy, or old links without `?cohort=` resolve to the cohort that holds the model's newest scores.
- Comparing across cohorts is possible behind the existing mixed-settings warning, or the UI says what to do instead.
- The compare and model links posted in #10695, #9920, #9984 and #10213 show scores again.

comments.body:
🤖
# Research

[EvalDash metadata](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e8eeba00da7aefd98b31620ad8d938e1d442d52d/infra/marina/apps/evaldash/metrics.py#L467-L496) hard-codes the September 24 default and omits null versions from the selector. [Request parsing](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e8eeba00da7aefd98b31620ad8d938e1d442d52d/infra/marina/apps/evaldash/app.py#L1304-L1309) treats a missing cohort as that default; [Compare](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e8eeba00da7aefd98b31620ad8d938e1d442d52d/infra/marina/apps/evaldash/app.py#L1384-L1399) rejects the all-cohort selection. The [Panel](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e8eeba00da7aefd98b31620ad8d938e1d442d52d/infra/marina/apps/evaldash/web/src/pages/PanelPage.vue#L43-L95) and [model view](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e8eeba00da7aefd98b31620ad8d938e1d442d52d/infra/marina/apps/evaldash/web/src/pages/ModelDetailPage.vue#L38-L56) then write the stale default into old links. [PR #10957](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10957) already removes the all-cohort Compare restriction and retains the mixed-settings warning, so that part should land there.

# Proposed Fix

1. After #10957, add an explicit `cohort=unversioned` selection through the API request type, record filtering, Panel/Compare selectors, and metadata. Keep `cohort=all` distinct; null-version records may span settings and must carry the existing unverified warning.
2. Make `cohort=all` the default for requests without a cohort, including Panel, Compare, and model links. Preserve explicit named cohorts in URLs. This makes old links resolve to each model's newest admissible benchmark scores without claiming a new verified policy.
3. Add API tests for named, unversioned, and all-cohort selection and comparison; add browser coverage for URL hydration and the warning. After deployment, check the shared links in #10695, #9920, #9984, and #10213 for visible scores. A verified October 16 cohort would require the launcher to stamp a policy label and publish its conformance contract; null versions alone cannot establish that contract.

This spans the API selection contract and three client views, with an active overlapping PR, so it should be implemented as a focused follow-up to #10957.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 Draft fix, as three stacked PRs:

1. #11131 lets Compare answer for the all-cohorts selection, keeping the mixed-settings warning.
2. #11132 adds `cohort=unversioned` for records with `version: null`, listed in the selector.
3. #11133 opens links without `?cohort=` on the newest result per benchmark across cohorts. This restores the links in #10695, #9920, #9984 and #10213 once EvalDash is next released.

Cause. #9461 (`bf0ca496ff`) made a missing cohort mean `eval-policy-2026-09-24-verified` (`app.py` `_selection`, `metrics.py` `build_meta`) and had the Panel and model pages write it into the URL. #9752 (`53e0aa1d11`) made `/compare` refuse the all-cohorts selection. #10965 did not change cohort handling. It requires policy records to land under the roots EvalDash scans.

On the labels: the 2026-10-16 policy is not the 09-24 policy in code. Each of the 26 current-policy v0.1 records, and each of the 26 A13 records, fails the 09-24 checks. Benchmark config digests differ, `swebench-verified` is not in the 09-24 policy, and the policy requires Evalchemy `c131e5ab`, seed 42 and fixed `max_gen_toks`. Relabeling them `eval-policy-2026-09-24-verified` would hide them as policy violations.

323 records already carry `eval-policy-2026-10-16-verified`. EvalDash lists that label without checks, because only versions with a definition in `eval_policy.py` are verified. Our v0.1 records match that cohort's benchmark config digests on 20 of 26 benchmarks. They differ on six Harbor benchmarks (BFCL, BixBench, DS-1000, SOTOPIA-hard, SWE-bench Verified, τ³). This was a sample of at most two tracker records per benchmark.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
On cw-rno2a at interactive priority, Kueue preempted the owned 8xH100 serve of a paired-maths screen three times in about an hour (2026-11-10 02:10–03:15 UTC). Each preemption failed the whole screen. Over the same window, a BFCL eval on the shared evaluation runner survived its own preemption. The difference is the harness, not the cluster.

The screen's driver submits its serve and its CPU evaluator jobs with `max_retries_preemption=0` and `max_retries_failure=0`: `experiments/post_training/identity_fullscreen_owner/owner.py` lines 82 (serve) and 225 (evaluators) on the branch `task/366-ws3-paired-math`. That is unpushed experiment code, not part of main. It overrides the `--max-retries-preemption` default of 10 in [`lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris_cli.py:394`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f6c200af77/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris_cli.py#L394). The driver also talks to the serve's capability URL directly, so it does not use the broker recovery from #10169. A preemption before readiness raises `Owned serve terminated before readiness`. A preemption after readiness turns every in-flight trial request into HTTP 502, and the driver does not resume partial trials.

## Which eval paths tolerate preemption

| Path | Preemption behavior | Tracking |
|---|---|---|
| Harbor / Evalchemy on `marin.evaluation.runner`, brokered serving | Pauses, waits for the replacement serve, resumes from saved output. BFCL survived a preemption on 2026-11-10. | #10169 (merged) |
| Direct capability-URL clients | The proxy returns 502 while Iris replaces the serve task. | #10273, fix in #10721 (open) |
| SkyRL eval-only runs | A kill before the last rollout writes no results. | #10837, fix in #10840 (open) |
| Iris retry after a sealed Evalchemy record | The retry can overwrite the sealed record. | #9972 |
| Eval driver pod itself evicted (Harbor groups, 2026-11-06 00:17 UTC, 106.0 H100-h; Echo incident record https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/961, Marina login required) | The group is lost; the serve recovery does not cover the driver. | none |
| Custom drivers that own a serve with preemption retries set to 0 (this report) | The first preemption is fatal. Partial trials are lost. | none |

## Reproduction

1. Run an experiment driver that submits a vLLM serve through `marin.inference.iris_cli` and overrides `max_retries_preemption=0`, then runs CPU evaluator jobs against the serve's capability URL.
2. Run it at interactive priority on cw-rno2a while higher-priority GPU work is queued.
3. Kueue evicts the serve pod (`WorkloadEvictedDueToPreempted`).
4. Before readiness, the driver raises `Owned serve terminated before readiness`. After readiness, the trials see HTTP 502 `upstream endpoint request failed` until their retries run out, and the root job fails with `Full screen has incomplete command coverage; available outputs retained`.

## Expected behavior

A preempted serve is replaced, and the eval resumes or reruns only the unfinished trials, as the brokered runner already does. A driver that needs a fixed serve attempt for provenance should record the attempt id instead of disabling preemption retries.

## Evidence (cw-rno2a, interactive band, 2026-11-10 UTC)

| Root job | Serve preempted | Outcome | H100-h |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/karan/pathb-paired-math-t334-proj-ct-r1-r1` | during vLLM engine init, before readiness | root FAILED 02:12:36 after 1m49s | 0.166 |
| `/karan/pathb-paired-math-t334-proj-ct-r1-r2` | 2m15s on node, before readiness | root failed after 20m06s | 0.301 |
| `/karan/pathb-paired-math-t334-soup3-r1` | 7m10s in, after readiness | all three trials failed on 502 | 0.957 |
| `/karan/eval-t334-proj-ct-r1-bfcl-run-01-8eccd44c` (control, brokered runner) | GPU attempt preempted at 27.8 s | replacement attempt started, run continued | — |

All three serve children report `WorkloadEvictedDueToPreempted: Preempted to accommodate a workload`. Retries were 0/0 on every failed serve.

## Time wasted

These numbers come from our preemption record for this campaign. They count every preempted attempt in our run ledgers, not just the three screens above.

**Allocation exposure, not proven irrecoverable work.** GPU-h lost below is requested GPUs × native physical attempt duration. It is not proof that all work/results were lost; partial outputs/checkpoints may survive. Actual wasted-work total and result-loss flags remain UNKNOWN without application-result evidence.

Known H100 allocation-exposure subtotal: **44464309/75000 = 592.857453333 H100-h**; 6 affected GPU windows have UNKNOWN bounds. Scope coverage is incomplete: 288 roots were absent from the hub; 32 have no recoverable native attempt archive. Never treat these as zero.

Known H100 exposure by original host-root priority band:
- UNKNOWN: 738347/28125 = 26.252337778 H100-h
- PRIORITY_BAND_PRODUCTION: 69253/11250 = 6.155822222 H100-h
- PRIORITY_BAND_INTERACTIVE: 42033697/75000 = 560.449293333 H100-h

Known H100 exposure by harness pattern (training/export kept separate):
- Harbor group: 1441913/2500 = 576.765200000 H100-h
- training/export/other (separate from eval patterns): 757717/450000 = 1.683815556 H100-h
- owned-serve driver: 46157/28125 = 1.641137778 H100-h
- broker+workers: 127673/10000 = 12.767300000 H100-h

2026-11-06 00:17Z five-group Harbor incident: **47718767/450000 = 106.041704444 H100-h**. This is a tagged subset of the overall total, not an additional charge. CPU root preemptions and killed GPU descendants are linked; CPU trigger rows contribute 0 GPU-h.

Ten largest rows by GPU-h:

| Job root | Cluster | Band | Diagnostic | GPU-h (allocation proxy) |

| `/karan/eval-20261105-094057-open-athena-Snowball-67B-A2B-SFT-Shootout-Contributor-Plain-v0.1-2026.10.22-a93c7339c5c24329ad01883ab6470d16-e342989c` | cw-rno2a | PRIORITY_BAND_INTERACTIVE | Parent job terminated; native parent-preemption teardown | 150.930528889 |

| `/karan/eval-20261105-223905-open-athena-Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A3-2026.10.30-10460a5f620146f8a5963b2ca8c62856-ab71bc7d` | cw-rno2a | PRIORITY_BAND_INTERACTIVE | Parent job terminated; native parent-preemption teardown | 13.001195556 |

Full record (93 rows): `/mnt/storage/karan-scratchpad/task-334/preemption-record-r1/preemptions.md`, sha256 `668d8e86de9e…`. Machine-readable copy: `preemptions.json` (sha256 `06ce208a7f91…`); manifest `sha256-manifest.json` (sha256 `88af65dc5033…`). These paths are on a team host, not public.

## Proposed fix

- Move the paired-maths screen onto `marin.evaluation.runner` with brokered serving, or keep Iris's default preemption retries on the owned serve and re-resolve the endpoint after a replacement.
- Make trials resumable: skip trials that already have a sealed result, and rerun only unfinished ones.
- For any driver that keeps preemption retries at 0, request `production` priority per launch with owner sign-off, or document that preemption is fatal.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

The paired-maths driver sets preemption retries to zero for its serve and CPU evaluators, then sends trials to the serve's capability URL. A serve eviction is therefore terminal for that driver, and unfinished trials have no replay point. The driver is absent from `main`, and `task/366-ws3-paired-math` is not published on GitHub; the shared evaluation runner already has broker and evaluator-attempt recovery from #10169. Open PR #10721 addresses the direct proxy's 502 response during replacement, but does not make this driver's trials resumable.

**Relevant code**
- [`iris_cli.py#L394`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f6c200af77357342016df8f8a559b1503f571ddc/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris_cli.py#L394) — default 10 preemption retries.
- [`runner.py#L114-L145`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f6c200af77357342016df8f8a559b1503f571ddc/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/runner.py#L114-L145) — wait and retry evaluator attempts.
- [`runner.py#L399-L434`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f6c200af77357342016df8f8a559b1503f571ddc/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/runner.py#L399-L434) — retry in the same output directory.
- [`serving_config.py#L267-L288`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f6c200af77357342016df8f8a559b1503f571ddc/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/serving_config.py#L267-L288) — broker for single-task eval serving.

# Proposed Fix

1. Publish the paired-maths driver and its trial output contract. Port it to the shared evaluation runner's `EvalExecutor`/broker path, and retain a nonzero serve preemption retry budget. Keep #10721 scoped to proxy responses.
2. Give each trial a stable identity covering the model, command, scoring configuration, and seed. Write a validated result durably before marking the trial complete; on an evaluator or owner restart, load completed trials and run only missing ones. Apply a nonzero preemption retry budget to the CPU jobs after this replay path exists.
3. Exercise serve eviction before readiness, serve eviction with requests in flight, and CPU evaluator eviction. Each case should finish the same trial set without duplicate scoring or lost completed results. Check that a retry cannot replace a sealed successful record, the failure tracked in #9972, before enabling parent-job retries.

This needs the unpublished driver and a replay contract, so it is larger than a safe isolated fix in the current checkout. No PR for the owner driver is open.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Support expert-block weight synchronization when policy training and vLLM inference share GPUs (`trainer.placement.colocate_all=true`). The current restriction prevents this transport from being used in colocated runs; those runs must use another supported transport or allocate separate inference GPUs.

The restriction remains on main at [`3a8e8a72681011012ebb59c0c1ed34688ad6fdea`](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/commit/3a8e8a72681011012ebb59c0c1ed34688ad6fdea):

- [`validate_expert_block_transport`](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/3a8e8a72681011012ebb59c0c1ed34688ad6fdea/marinskyrl/inference_placement.py#L16-L63) explicitly rejects `colocate_all=true` for `generator.weight_sync_transport=expert_block`.
- [The inference-engine factory](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/3a8e8a72681011012ebb59c0c1ed34688ad6fdea/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/inference_engines/ray_wrapped_inference_engine.py#L594-L602) excludes hybrid/shared-GPU and sleeping engines from verified receiver placement, then rejects expert-block synchronization without those placements.

This is a confirmed implementation restriction from source inspection, not evidence that GPU colocation is fundamentally incompatible with expert-block transfer. No new GPU experiment was run for this issue. [Marin #10333](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10333) adds an early launcher rejection for the existing restriction; it does not implement support.

Done when:

- At least one documented colocated MoE Megatron/vLLM configuration can complete training, expert-block synchronization, and generation across repeated updates. An initial subset of parallelism configurations is sufficient.
- Receiver placement checks account for shared physical GPUs and worker lifecycle. Sleep/offload modes may remain unsupported initially if explicitly rejected; any supported mode needs transition coverage.
- GPU tests compare transferred weights and fixed-input logits against a fresh vLLM load of the same updated checkpoint, with documented numerical tolerances, and detect stale or misrouted weights.
- Non-colocated transfer remains covered, unsupported combinations fail before GPU allocation, and the documented support matrix and Marin launcher guard agree with the implemented support.


Transferred from https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/issues/1033.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

The vendored SkyRL config rejects `expert_block` with `colocate_all=true`, and the engine factory omits shared-GPU workers from verified receiver placement. The colocated update path wakes weights and syncs without setting the generation-paused state required by `ExpertBlockSync.sync()`; startup also puts engines to sleep before `prepare()` collects receiver inventories. These are implementation barriers, not evidence that shared GPUs cannot transfer the blocks; no colocated GPU run has validated the path.

**Relevant code**
- [Transport validation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ea93941256996206691eef58f29e8b0fa7fa5060/vendor/skyrl/marinskyrl/inference_placement.py#L16-L63) — rejects colocation before launch.
- [Engine placement gate](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ea93941256996206691eef58f29e8b0fa7fa5060/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/inference_engines/ray_wrapped_inference_engine.py#L594-L602) — excludes hybrid and sleeping engines.
- [Engine startup](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ea93941256996206691eef58f29e8b0fa7fa5060/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/inference_engines/ray_wrapped_inference_engine.py#L973-L1025) — reports placement or sleeps, then records receivers.
- [Expert-block driver](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ea93941256996206691eef58f29e8b0fa7fa5060/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/weight_sync/expert_block/driver.py#L151-L203) — prepares receivers and requires paused generation.
- [Colocated update](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ea93941256996206691eef58f29e8b0fa7fa5060/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/trainer.py#L1185-L1217) — wakes, syncs, offloads, then wakes KV cache.

# Design

Enable one bounded colocated configuration first: a single-node Megatron MoE policy with TP=ETP=1 and EP=4, one local vLLM engine with TP=PP=1 and DP=EP=4 on the same four GPUs, NCCL expert-block transport, and vLLM sleep level 1. Keep other parallelism and sleep/offload combinations rejected before GPU allocation. This needs a four-GPU model small enough to leave room for the weight-wake/transfer phase; memory fit and communicator survival are GPU acceptance criteria, not assumptions.

## Challenges and risks

The current verified-placement path builds receiver evidence from dedicated inference placement groups, while colocation uses the trainer's shared group. Sleeping can also discard receiver tensors or NCCL state. A successful first transfer would not establish that later updates reach the right expert ranks or that the receiver survives another train/sleep/wake cycle.

## Implementation

1. Extend placement reporting to the shared placement group. Match each receiver's reported host, GPU UUID, DP/EP rank, and bundle to the actual allocation; allow its GPU UUID to match a trainer rank while still requiring distinct receiver GPUs and unique receiver ranks. Recheck after an actor restart or placement change.
2. Define the supported lifecycle in the trainer: pause and drain generation at the rollout boundary, sleep engines for training, wake receiver weights after training, prepare or rebuild expert-block groups while receivers are live, transfer and verify the current version, release policy memory, wake KV cache, then resume generation. Reconcile startup `prepare()` with the initial sleep barrier and tear down or rebuild groups if sleep invalidates them. Fail the update without resuming generation when placement or version verification fails.
3. Gate only the tested configuration in `validate_expert_block_transport` and the Marin launcher. Coordinate with [#10333](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10333), which adds the current early rejection, and reuse the non-colocated GPU harness from [#10377](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10377) after it lands. Update the support matrix and an exact runnable config with the same constraints.

## Testing

Add CPU tests for shared-group placement, duplicate/misrouted receiver identity, unsupported config rejection before engine creation, and pause/wake failure behavior. On four GPUs, run at least two training updates with a tiny MoE model; after each transfer compare selected dense and per-expert tensors plus fixed-input logits to a fresh vLLM load of that update's checkpoint. Record and justify numerical tolerances, change different expert blocks between updates to expose stale or swapped weights, and generate after each wake. Retain the non-colocated transfer test and run the launch guard against both supported and rejected configs.

## Open question

Does level-1 sleep free enough GPU memory while preserving the receiver and NCCL groups for the target four-GPU layout? If the probe fails, keep colocation rejected while implementing an explicit level-2 wake/rebuild path and repeat the same GPU gate before enabling it.

issues.author: muchanem
issues.body:
Sub-issue of #8366; builds on #8415, #8416, #8417. `_compute_file_pushdown` (`plan.py:517`) runs only when a pipeline starts with a `LoadFileOp`. The dominant production form is `Dataset.from_list(entries).flat_map(load_file)`: normalize uses it for every datakit source (`normalize.py:386-397`) and the fast-transformer scorer uses it deliberately to prevent shard splitting (`score.py:177-181`, docstring at `:21-23`). Reader pushdown, filter-lambda lowering (#8416), and projection inference (#8417) therefore never reach the highest-volume pipelines.

Plan: canonicalize the shape at plan time. When the source is a list of paths or `InputFileSpec`s and the first op is a `flat_map` over `load_file`/`load_parquet`/`load_file_batch` (bare or a `functools.partial` with supported kwargs such as `include_file_paths`), rewrite to the `LoadFileOp`-headed plan so the existing pushdown pass and the callable-analysis path apply. Constraints: a hand-built `InputFileSpec` keeps its columns and filter — pushdown may narrow them, never widen or replace; task granularity is preserved (one task per list entry, no `approx_shard_bytes` splitting introduced, so the scorer's no-split rationale holds); unsupported partial kwargs, mixed entry types, or non-loader callables bail to current behavior.

Done when:
Normalize-shaped and scorer-shaped pipelines, replicated in zephyr tests without importing marin, carry spec-level filter and projection pushdown under the callable-analysis flag with outputs identical to the unlowered run; hand-built spec lists are preserved and only narrowed; unsupported shapes bail cleanly. Lands in the stacked PR series ending the campaign.

issues.author: muchanem
issues.body:
Sub-issue of #8366; builds on #8415. Callers read every column and use a few: exact dedup hashes id and text with no `columns=` (`exact.py:155`), the fast-transformer scorer reads full rows for id and truncated text (`score.py:177`), normalize `bare=True` keeps only id, text, and source_id after loading everything (`normalize.py:161`). The luxical pipeline measured ~120 GB saved at 15B-document scale by dropping one column (`luxical/pipeline.py:352`).

Projection needs no semantic understanding of the callable, only the set of keys it can access, and a superset is always safe. Plan: static analysis of `map`/`flat_map`/`filter` callables in the pushdown pass. When every row access is a literal subscript or `.get` and the row does not escape (no `**r`, `dict(r)`, iteration, `.keys()`, passing the row to another call), the accessed-key set becomes `columns=` on the `InputFileSpec`. Any escape bails out to full projection. Filter-column widening (`readers.py:296`) is unchanged. This covers `map` and `flat_map`, which predicate lowering (#8416) cannot reach.

Done when:
Inference runs behind the same opt-in as #8416, escape bail-out is covered by tests, and the three sites above scan only their accessed columns. Lands in the stacked PR series ending the campaign.

issues.author: muchanem
issues.body:
Sub-issue of #8366; builds on #8415. No production pipeline imports `zephyr.expr`: every `Dataset.filter` in `lib/marin` and `experiments/` passes a Python lambda, so `_compute_file_pushdown` (`plan.py:517`) stops at the first op and reader pushdown never fires.

A pushed predicate can precede the lambda instead of replacing it. The lambda still runs on rows that survive the scan, so the derived expression only has to hold whenever the lambda returns True. Extraction can therefore be conservative:

- Analyze the filter callable at plan time with `inspect.getsource` and `ast` over a closed subset: comparisons, `and`/`or`/`not`, `in` on literal collections, `is None`, literal subscripts, `.get(k)`, closure-variable resolution. Filters in this repo are module-level functions and lambdas, so source is available.
- For `A and B` where only A is expressible, push A. For `A or B`, push both or nothing. Bail out on anything unrecognized.
- SQL filters drop rows where the predicate is NULL; Python does not (`r["x"] != 5` keeps a None row, `col("x") != 5` drops it). Push `col("x").is_null() | expr` so NULL means keep.
- Ship warn-and-suggest first (polars' BytecodeParser precedent: report the equivalent expression, let the author rewrite), then enable pushing behind an opt-in flag.

Validation reuses the differential harness from #8415: generate lambdas from the supported grammar and assert every row the lambda keeps also passes the pushed expression.

Sites that lower today: `has_text` (`normalize.py:377`), the diagnostic-logs partition equality (`diagnostic_logs.py:870`), the common_corpus language and open-type filters (`common_corpus.py:57`), the numinamath validity flags (`numinamath_v1_5.py:50`).

Done when:
Warn mode reports lowerable filters, the opt-in flag pushes them with outputs identical to the unpushed run, the property suite covers the supported grammar, and the four sites above prune under the flag. Lands in the stacked PR series ending the campaign.

issues.author: mcwitt
issues.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

Marin EP is an experimental Grug MoE backend for the GB200 hero: group-pooled waterfilling acceptance plus fused Mosaic-GPU transport, now working multi-process in the production 1-process/GPU topology. Upstream replaced NVSHMEM with the NCCL device API via collective metadata; with a patched PJRT wheel (kMaxPeers-128 + two 4096-alignment fixes), `--xla_gpu_enable_dynamic_slice_fusion=false`, and a separate collective allocator, the fused transport trains conformantly across nodes. The current EP64 hero best is 17.0 s/step, ~247k tokens/s/rack (~22.6% MFU) at 0.5-0.6% drops — from 18.1 s at the start of the campaign — via fused transport (17.75), Pallas Blackwell ragged-dot expert GEMMs (17.08, ~1.6x the QuACK/cuDNN path), and per-leg kernel configs (17.0). A correctness bug was found on the way: the cuDNN grouped Wgrad silently miscomputes unless group offsets are 64-aligned (#8339, fixed on the measurement branch). Profiles show the remaining 5 s to the 25% / 350k gate sits in attention/dense GEMMs, XLA fusion mass, and FSDP one-shot collectives rather than the MoE path.

### Helpful links
- Latest EP64 ladder + profile: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8311#issuecomment-5309381342 and https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8311#issuecomment-5309484707
- Multi-process transport unblock (three XLA findings + fixes): https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8311#issuecomment-5308550100
- Wgrad correctness bug: #8339; barrier-bound context: #8077, #8313, openxla/xla#47283
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description

Experimental fused expert-parallel MoE backend for `moe_hero_ep` (d6144, 192 latent experts, top-4, EP64 on GB200 NVL72), developed simulator-first against a dense oracle: behavior spec, NumPy oracle, message-passing correctness simulator with explicit backward, and L0/L1 performance models before hardware. The backend lives in `levanter.grug._moe.ep_marin` (+ `marin_ep_transport`); spec and research artifacts under `experiments/marin_ep/`. Branch `marin-ep`. This is an experimental backend: it has not run a full-scale training gate and is not a production default.

Differences from `fixed_all_to_all`/`ragged_all_to_all`:

- Acceptance is deterministic group-pooled waterfilling over global expert counts, pooling capacity across each owner's co-located experts. It is EP-degree invariant and drops 0.31% at cf 1.33 under hero-calibrated skew, vs ~4% for the per-cell rule at the same buffer bytes.
- Transport is one generic Mosaic-GPU put kernel (`put_segments`) that writes each owner's expert-major receive pool directly, eliminating both local permutes; dispatch and combine plans are transposes of each other, so the backward runs the same kernel with the opposite plan (custom_vjp).

## Hypothesis or Goal

Reach >= 25% MFU and >= 350k tokens/s/rack at the hero shape with EP64, keeping drops < 2% in the trained-router regime. Baseline `fixed_all_to_all`: 24.04% MFU, 262,683 tok/s at cf 1.30 with 3.96% drops.

## Status

- Multi-process fused transport validated end-to-end: 8-rank cross-node conformance (values, drops bit-identical to the ragged path, all gradients at the bf16 floor), then EP16 proxy (17.0 s vs 18.05 flat) and EP64 hero. Requires the patched PJRT wheel `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/research/mcwitt-ra2a/pjrt-kmax128-align4096-dev0811-20260816/` and `--xla_gpu_enable_dynamic_slice_fusion=false`; an upstream report of the three XLA findings is drafted pending review.
- EP64 hero ladder (25-step runs, same wheel/flags, single draws +/-2pp): brd 17.0 s/step (~247k tok/s, ~22.6% MFU, 0.5-0.6% drops) < mgpu-cute 17.75 < flat ragged 18.0. Flavors `ep-marin-mgpu-brd` / `ep-marin-mgpu-cudnn-cute` on branch `marin-ep-8081`.
- Expert GEMMs now run on jax's Pallas Blackwell ragged-dot kernel (fwd + dgrad; 1195-1531 TF/s per leg at true hero shapes, ~1.6x the QuACK/cuDNN path) with the 64-alignment-fixed cuDNN grouped wgrad (#8339). Hero dims need N-padding to the collective tile (2I=6272, I=3136).
- Dead ends recorded: PGLE OOMs on the fused flavor (its profiling pass falls back to dense a2a); command buffers neutral; scoped ragged groups and the hierarchical two-hop transport slower than flat; a memory-bound fused consumer hides only ~7% (M7a) — expert-major send order is the overlap lever, and M7b targets gating the ragged-dot group scheduler on arrival flags.
- Remaining gap to 25% MFU / 350k tok/s: ~5 s/step in attention/dense GEMMs (4.9 s busy), XLA fusions (3.5 s), and FSDP one-shot collectives (2.8 s + 1.05 s barriers) — outside the EP transport scope; fp8 wire + attention/fusion work are the ranked candidates.

## Links

* Logbook: `.agents/logbooks/marin-ep.md` (entries MEP-001..MEP-044; measurement branch `marin-ep-8081`, PR branch `marin-ep` / #8320)
* Plan: `.agents/projects/20260814_marin_ep_kernel.md`; M7 plan: `.agents/projects/marin-ep-m7.md`; spec: `experiments/marin_ep/SPEC.md`
* W&B: marin-community/marin_moe (runs `mep-*-20260815/16`)

## Decision Log

- 2026-08-14: adopted group-pooled waterfilling (pool group = experts per device) into the spec; per-cell and per-expert pooling both leave ~4% drops at cf 1.33.
- 2026-08-14: transport substrate = Pallas Mosaic-GPU remote puts + arrival semaphores (584 GB/s/device untuned on one tray, zero custom CUDA).
- 2026-08-15: multi-controller runs fall back to ragged transport after pinning the upstream NVSHMEM removal; hierarchical transport is the planned successor.

- 2026-08-16: multi-process fused transport adopted (collective metadata + patched wheel + dynamic-slice-fusion off) after the NVSHMEM-removal block proved obsolete; hierarchical transport retired.
- 2026-08-16: expert activation-path GEMMs moved to jax's Pallas Blackwell ragged-dot kernel; cuDNN grouped wgrad kept with the 64-alignment fix (#8339).

## Conclusion

comments.body:
🤖 Update: multi-process fused transport is viable again — cross-node spike passes on the NCCL device API / collective-metadata path; full-layer integration blocked by an XLA alignment bug with a patched-wheel fix in progress

- Change: re-tested the fused `put_segments` transport in the production multi-process topology (1 process/GPU) after discovering that upstream did not drop multi-process Mosaic remote copies when it removed NVSHMEM — it replaced the backend with the NCCL Device API served through collective metadata (jax commit 181661c3a5: "XLA is deprecating NVSHMEM. Instead of NVSHMEM customers should use NCCL Device API through collective metadata"; the multi-process distributed test was migrated, not deleted).
- Result delta:
  - Standalone transport smoke, 2 GB200 nodes x 4 GPUs, 8 processes, stock dev20260809 nightly, no NVSHMEM, no extra XLA flags: all 8 ranks bit-exact against the plan reference, per-rank egress 153-209 GB/s through the fused puts. The earlier "fused transport is single-process-only" conclusion is obsolete, and the hierarchical fallback is no longer the only route to cross-node fused transport.
  - Full-layer conformance smoke (forward+backward with `transport="mgpu"` forced): fails at first execution with NCCL `Window address must be suitably aligned`. Root cause: with more than one Mosaic collective kernel per executable, at least one kernel parameter escapes XLA's collective-memory-space analysis and gets window-registered from the default arena at XLA's 256-byte packing alignment; NCCL windows require 4096-byte alignment. Single-kernel programs pass by accident of allocation layout, which is why the transport smoke and the upstream test are green.
- Fix in progress: rebuilding `jax-cuda13-pjrt` at the same pins as the kMaxPeers-128 wheel with one additional one-line patch (buffer-assignment alignment 256 -> 4096) so every registrable offset is aligned. If the layer smoke passes on the patched wheel, next steps are an `ep-marin-mgpu-cudnn-cute` hero flavor, the EP16 proxy, and the EP64 A/B against the 18.1 s/step ragged recipe; an openxla/xla issue with the repro and validated patch will follow.
- Confidence: transport-smoke results replicated on two nightlies (dev20260809, dev20260816); alignment diagnosis is from instrumented window-registration logs (pointer/size identify the offending buffer) plus a bisected minimal repro.
- Links:
  - Logbook: `.agents/logbooks/marin-ep.md` MEP-030..031 (branch `marin-ep-8081`)

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
**What is this document?** This document is an attempt to formalize Marin’s policy towards what constitutes reportable, public-facing, canonical eval results for Marin models as well as the baselines we compare against.

**Why do we need this document?** With the first “snowball” cool-down, Marin is entering a regime where we regularly compare Marin models to existing open and closed-source models. Because Marin’s unique claim is that we are open development, we will need to hold ourselves to a high standard of transparency on how we report eval scores of Marin models and what claims we make about Marin model capabilities based on those scores.

**What is in scope for this document?** This document is intended to act as a living snapshot, trustworthy for any given period in time, as to the *what* and the *how* of Marin’s canonical set of evals. By what, we mean “which evals did we run, with what consistent set of hyperparameters and experimental constraints”. By how, we mean “where is the self-contained codebase that is both necessary and sufficient to reproduce our eval results independently”.

**What is not in scope for this document?** Everything else. More explicitly, this policy will not cover bespoke, custom “val set” evals we use for data mixing, RL, etc., which can have distinct pipelines; it will not cover what benchmarks we should add or remove from the in-distribution (hill-climbed) set in the future; it’s not for roadmapping or future planning; and it will not cover how we present results or talk about them in public.

## How

Use [Running Evaluations with Marin](https://marin.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/run-lm-evals/) as the launch runbook. The [source on `main`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/docs/tutorials/run-lm-evals.md) tracks the current launcher, model registry, suites, placement, durable records, and result inspection. Use [Harbor evaluation](https://marin.readthedocs.io/en/latest/harbor-integration/) for supplied Harbor `JobConfig` files and Daytona credentials.

Routine post-hoc evaluations use the shared launcher:

```bash
uv run python -m experiments.evaluation.cli launch \
  --model <registered-model-key> \
  --evals <registered-suite-or-eval-keys> \
  --dry-run
```

Remove `--dry-run` after the plan resolves the intended model, tasks, accelerator, target cluster or region, and records prefix.

Interactive in-distribution agentic evaluations use SWE-bench-verified random-100, Terminal-Bench 2.0, and OT-TBLite in one launch:

```bash
uv run python -m experiments.evaluation.cli launch \
  --model <registered-model-key> \
  --evals swebench,tb2,grug-opencode-id \
  --priority interactive \
  --no-wait
```

`grug-opencode-id` is the current registry key for OT-TBLite (`DCAgent/dev_set_v2`). [#8150](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8150) tracks replacing it with `ot-tblite`; update the command when that key lands.

### Eval tracks

| Track | Measures | Framework | Selection |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Non-agentic | Single-turn generation or loglikelihood | Evalchemy + lm-eval-harness | `--evals <registered-suite-or-eval-keys>` |
| Agentic (registered) | Tool use, coding, multi-turn agent rollout scoring | Harbor | `--evals <registered-harbor-key>` |
| Agentic (supplied policy) | Tool use, coding, multi-turn agent rollout scoring | Harbor | `--harbor-config <job.yaml>` |

`--evals` accepts only entries from `experiments/evaluation/evals.py` and its named suites. `--harbor-config` is repeatable and accepts supported external Harbor YAML or JSON policies. File-backed Evalchemy and lm-eval definitions are not supported; [#7990](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7990) tracks that follow-up.

## What

### Benchmark suite

**Status legend:** ✅ production-ready · 🔧 in development (PR open) · ⚠️ has known issues · ❌ not started

**AA-II column:** Maps each benchmark to the AA-II component(s) it serves as a surrogate for (see [AA-II proxy weights](#aa-ii-proxy-weights) below). “—” means the benchmark is a canonical baseline outside the AA-II scheme.

#### Evalchemy chat benchmarks (`eval.eval`)

| Benchmark | Metric | Seeds | AA-II component | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MATH500 | pass@1 | 1 (42) | — | ✅ | |
| AIME24 | pass@1 (mean ± std) | 10 (42–51) | — | ✅ | |
| HumanEvalPlus | pass@1 | 1 (42) | — | ✅ | |
| MBPPPlus | pass@1 | 1 (42) | — | ✅ | |
| OlympiadBench | exact match | 1 (42) | HLE (math) + CritPt (physics) | ⚠️ | PR #24 merged; multi-part scoring + tolerance handling needs follow-up (vendor official `auto_scoring_judge.py`) |
| MMLU-Pro | accuracy | 1 (42) | HLE | ⚠️ | Issue #32: dataset download failure on some configs |
| GPQA Diamond | accuracy | 1 (42) | GPQA Diamond | ✅ | |
| CruxEval | accuracy | 1 (42) | SciCode | ⚠️ | Issue #33: import error (`CruxEvalTask` references unavailable module) |
| FinanceBench | LLM judge (SimpleQA-style) | 1 (42) | GDPval-AA v2 | 🔧 | PR #25: rewritten with real `patronus-ai/financebench` evidence text, awaiting review |
| IFBench | constraint verification (AI2 graders) | 1 (42) | GDPval-AA v2 | 🔧 | PR #23: rewritten with real `allenai/IFBench_test` + vendored 58-constraint graders, awaiting review |
| MRCR | SequenceMatcher ratio | 1 (42) | AA-LCR | 🔧 | PR #22: rewritten with real `openai/mrcr` (2,400 rows, 2/4/8-needle bins), awaiting review. Non-agentic long-context benchmark—runs via evalchemy, **not** harbor |

Pass `--verbosity INFO` and `--max_tokens` (not `--gen_kwargs`).

#### lm-eval-harness tasks (`lm_eval` CLI)

| Task | Shots | Metric | AA-II component | Notes |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| `gsm8k` | 0 | `exact_match` | — | Run via `lm_eval`, **not** `eval.eval` (double-engine OOM) |
| `mmlu` | 5 | `acc` | — | |
| `hellaswag` | 10 | `acc_norm` | — | |
| `arc_challenge` | 25 | `acc_norm` | — | |
| `arc_easy` | 0 | `acc_norm` | — | |
| `piqa` | 0 | `acc_norm` | — | |
| `winogrande` | 5 | `acc` | — | |
| `openbookqa` | 0 | `acc_norm` | — | |
| `boolq` | 0 | `acc` | — | |
| `truthfulqa_mc2` | 0 | `acc` | — | |
| `lambada_openai` | 0 | `acc` | — | |
| `triviaqa` | 5 | `exact_match` | AA-Omniscience (alt) | Alternative surrogate for AA-Omniscience (primary = SimpleQA) |
| `nq_open` | 5 | `exact_match` | — | |
| `drop` | 3 | `f1` | — | |

1 run, seed 42.

#### Harbor (agentic through the shared launcher)

| Benchmark | `--preset` | Dataset | `n_concurrent` | AA-II component | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| SWE-bench-verified random-100 | `swebench` | `DCAgent/swebench_verified_eval_set` | 32 | — | ✅ | |
| OT-TBLite (`dev_set_v2`) | `v2` | `DCAgent/dev_set_v2` | 128 | Terminal-Bench | ✅ | Primary Terminal-Bench surrogate |
| Terminal-Bench 2.0 | `tb2` | `DCAgent2/terminal_bench_2` | 64 | — | ✅ | |
| τ²-Bench-Verified Retail | — | — | — | τ³-Banking | 🔧 | Harbor PR #10: functional skeleton adapter (114 tasks, MCP runtime), needs review approval |
| BFCL (Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard) | — | `adapters/bfcl` | — | τ³-Banking (alt) | ✅ | BFCL v4 single-turn + live (3,641 tasks, 13 categories). Harbor adapter at `adapters/bfcl/`; parity sample via `generate_parity_sample.py`. Alternative surrogate for τ³-Banking |
| SimpleQA | — | `harbor simpleqa` | — | AA-Omniscience | ✅ | +1/0/−1 scoring. Primary AA-Omniscience surrogate |
| DS-1000 | — | `harbor ds-1000` | — | SciCode + GDPval-AA v2 | ✅ | |

Use a registered Harbor key with `--evals`, or pass one `--harbor-config` file per dataset. The benchmark table remains canonical when a file-backed config is required. ID mean = average per-benchmark z-score over SWE/`dev_set_v2`/`tb2` (`dev_set_v2` excluded from SE/ranking). Tool-using models require the correct `tool_call_parser`. Daytona uses `DAYTONA_API_KEY`, with the approved `DAYTONA_EVAL_API_KEY` secret as the launcher fallback.

#### pass@k (standalone vLLM driver)

`passatk_driver.py`—one batched `llm.generate(SamplingParams(n=128, temperature=0.7, seed=42))`, sub-sample k ∈ {1, 8, 32, 128}.

Estimator: `pass@k = mean[1 − C(n−c,k)/C(n,k)]`.

#### Shared rules

- **Runs per benchmark:** 3. Run every benchmark 3 times (seeds 42, 43, 44); report the mean.

- **Decoding:** `temperature=0.7`, `top_p=1.0`, `num_fewshot=0`, `repetition_penalty=1.1`. Applied consistently across all frameworks.

- **Context length:** standard = 32k (`max-model-len=32768`); extended = 131k. Set `max_gen_toks=32768` (standard) or `131072` (extended). Shared across all frameworks.

- **Reasoning parser:** every model, every benchmark—verify the correct reasoning parser (e.g. `hermes`, `deepseek_r1`) is configured and applied for models that emit `<think>`/reasoning tokens.

- **Chat template:** Ensure the correct template via `--apply_chat_template` (override to the correct template, e.g. `delphi_v0.jinja2`) whenever templates are available.

- **Logging:** `--log_samples` always on; set `--output_path` to durable storage (never `/tmp`). Never pair with `--predict_only`. Per-sample records for **lm-eval-native** tasks persist correctly as of evalchemy **#28** (`676fb85f`, merged 2026-07-19)—before that the flag was accepted but native-task samples weren’t written (blocked offline rescoring, e.g. the `drop` re-score).

### Report format

| Suite | Row format |
| --- | --- |
| Math | `scale \| mix \| stage \| model \| MATH500 \| AIME24(mean/std) \| gsm8k \| notes` |
| NLP | `model \| params \| MMLU \| HellaSwag \| ARC-c \| ARC-e \| PIQA \| WinoGrande \| OBQA \| BoolQ \| TruthfulQA \| LAMBADA \| TriviaQA \| NQ \| DROP \| template` |
| Agentic | `model \| SWE-100 \| dev_set_v2 \| tb2 \| ID mean \| ID SE \| traces` |
| pass@k | `model \| type \| p@1 \| p@8 \| p@32 \| p@128 \| n \| job \| status` |

### Quality gate + re-fire discipline

**Gate:** A leg registers iff valid-complete ≥ 90% and non-benign ≤ 10% (use `scripts/database/eval_guardrail.py`). `AgentTimeout` is benign (passthrough-scored, counts as valid-complete)—do not flag on timeout rate. Benchmarks are resumed until valid-complete ≥ 90%. For certain publication-quality results, we should consider setting this gate even higher, perhaps >95% or >99%.

> **Technical note:** Harbor main already has rich error classification and resume capability. Evalchemy is currently less mature. [evalchemy PR #19](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/pull/19) tracks the attempt to create similar infra-aware gating in Evalchemy.

### AA-II proxy weights

| Component | Weight | Surrogate(s) | Surrogate status |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| GDPval-AA v2 | 20% | FinanceBench + IFBench + DS-1000 | FinanceBench 🔧 · IFBench 🔧 · DS-1000 ✅ |
| τ³-Banking | 14% | τ²-Bench-Verified Retail (or BFCL, or a small BFCL parity subset) | τ²-Bench-Verified Retail 🔧 · BFCL ✅ |
| Terminal-Bench | 16% | OT-TBLite | ✅ |
| SciCode | 8% | DS-1000 + CruxEval | DS-1000 ✅ · CruxEval ⚠️ |
| HLE | 12% | MMLU-Pro + OlympiadBench (math) | MMLU-Pro ⚠️ · OlympiadBench ⚠️ |
| GPQA Diamond | 6% | GPQA Diamond | ✅ |
| CritPt | 6% | OlympiadBench (physics) | ⚠️ |
| AA-Omniscience | 12% | SimpleQA or TriviaQA | SimpleQA ✅ · TriviaQA ✅ |
| AA-LCR | 6% | MRCR | 🔧 |

Composite replacements: normalize each constituent, macro-average within the component, then apply weight. Publish every component alongside the aggregate.

**Coverage gaps:** MRCR, FinanceBench, and IFBench have open PRs awaiting review. CruxEval, MMLU-Pro, and OlympiadBench have known issues blocking production use. Until these are resolved, the corresponding AA-II components cannot be fully computed.

issues.author: ravwojdyla-agent
issues.body:
`step_lock` detects a lost lease within one heartbeat, but only acts on it after the step body has finished. The heartbeat sets `lease_lost_event` and returns; the event is read in the `finally` block, which runs after `yield status_file` returns. The step keeps computing until it completes on its own, then fails on release.

https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/step_status.py#L262-L285

```python
    def _heartbeat():
        while not stop_event.wait(HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL):
            try:
                status_file.refresh_lock()
            except LeaseLostError:
                logger.error("Lease lost for %s — step must terminate", output_path, exc_info=True)
                lease_lost_event.set()
                return
    ...
    try:
        yield status_file
    finally:
        stop_event.set()
        heartbeat_thread.join(timeout=5)
        if lease_lost_event.is_set():
            raise LeaseLostError(f"Lease was lost during execution of {output_path}")
```

The log line says "step must terminate", but nothing terminates it.

## Observed cost

Two Datakit tokenize drivers ran against one shared output store, on `cw-us-east-02a` and `cw-rno2a`. For `datakit/tokenize/nemotron_cc_v2/high_quality_synthetic_ad8827c1` (8778 shards), the Reno driver logged:

```
13:19:47  Acquired lock for datakit/tokenize/nemotron_cc_v2/high_quality_synthetic_ad8827c1
23:00:44  Lease lost for s3://…/high_quality_synthetic_ad8827c1 — step must terminate
03:09:47  Step datakit/tokenize/nemotron_cc_v2/high_quality_synthetic_ad8827c1 succeeded in 13:49:58
03:09:47  Step failed: datakit/tokenize/nemotron_cc_v2/high_quality_synthetic_ad8827c1
          LeaseLostError: Lease was lost during execution of s3://…/high_quality_synthetic_ad8827c1
```

Reno held a 128-worker pool for 10 hours 9 minutes after losing the lease, redoing work the East driver was already committing. The same shape occurred on `datakit/tokenize/nemotron_cc_v2/diverse_qa_3ed484fe`.

The final artifacts are correct: both steps end `SUCCESS` with complete output (8778 of 8778 shards for `high_quality_synthetic`). This is wasted compute and a misleading `Step failed` at the end of a step whose work did finish, not data loss.

## Suggested direction

Make lease loss cancel the in-flight work rather than only fail at release. The detection already exists; it needs a path to the runner. For zephyr-backed steps that means aborting the pipeline, so the worker pool is released promptly instead of at the natural end of the step.

Distinguishing the two outcomes at the call site would also help: a step that lost its lease because another worker committed the same output is not the same failure as a step whose work failed. The first is expected under concurrent drivers and should not count against a run's failure budget.

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

`step_lock` records lease loss in a thread event, but it reads the event only after the step body returns. `run_step` can then write `SUCCESS` or `FAILED` before `step_lock` raises `LeaseLostError`. The affected Datakit driver shares one Zephyr pool across concurrent steps, so a pool-wide abort would stop unrelated work.

**Relevant code**
- [`step_status.py#L241-L283`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/64913f5302e207098a01d4c6d8948f1dbe927e29/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/step_status.py#L241-L283) - Lease-loss event lifecycle
- [`step_runner.py#L431-L475`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/64913f5302e207098a01d4c6d8948f1dbe927e29/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/step_runner.py#L431-L475) - Status writes and outcome
- [`execution.py#L614-L629`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/64913f5302e207098a01d4c6d8948f1dbe927e29/lib/zephyr/src/zephyr/execution.py#L614-L629) - Shared pipeline execution
- [`coordinator.py#L1058-L1071`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/64913f5302e207098a01d4c6d8948f1dbe927e29/lib/zephyr/src/zephyr/coordinator.py#L1058-L1071) - Pool-wide abort
- [`runners.py#L396-L476`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/64913f5302e207098a01d4c6d8948f1dbe927e29/lib/zephyr/src/zephyr/runners.py#L396-L476) - Subprocess lifecycle

# Proposed Fix

## Outcome

Lease loss will cancel work before the step body returns. The losing driver will wait for the winning result without a failure-budget charge.

## Challenges

A Python thread cannot safely stop another Python thread. Zephyr can stop its isolated shard subprocesses, but an active `InlineRunner` shard needs cooperative cancellation.

The Datakit reference driver shares one Zephyr pool across steps. Cancellation must select one execution and keep other executions active.

## Costs / Risks

- The change adds a small cancellation API to Rigging.
- The Zephyr worker will track each active runner by execution ID.
- An `InlineRunner` abort will stop queued shards, but its active shard can finish before teardown.
- A remote abort can fail during a controller outage. The driver will still preserve the lease-loss outcome.

## Design

Rigging will provide a thread-safe `CancellationToken` and a context-local cancellation scope. A token accepts callback registration and calls each callback once when cancellation occurs.

`step_lock` will create the token before it starts the heartbeat. The yielded step body will run in that token scope. A `LeaseLostError` from `refresh_lock()` will cancel the token immediately.

`_submit_iris_job()` will register `JobHandle.terminate()` with the current token. Thus, lease loss will stop a remote Fray job while `handle.wait()` blocks.

`ZephyrContext` will register an abort callback for each `execution_id`. The callback will call a new `ZephyrCoordinator.abort_execution(execution_id, reason)` API.

The coordinator will mark only that execution as failed and clear its queued shards. It will ask only workers with that execution's in-flight shards to cancel their runners.

`ZephyrWorker` will track active runners by execution ID. A new `cancel_execution(execution_id)` method will call `StageRunner.cancel()` for matching runners.

`SubprocessRunner` will use `Popen` and retain the active child handle. Its `cancel()` method will terminate that child process. `InlineRunner.cancel()` cannot stop user Python code, so the coordinator will drain that active shard.

`run_step` will inspect the cancellation token before each terminal status write. It will not write `FAILED` or `SUCCESS` after lease loss.

After cancellation, `run_step` will enter lock acquisition again. It will wait for the current owner, return after `SUCCESS`, or retry after a real owner failure.

## Contract

```python
class CancellationToken:
    @property
    def cancelled(self) -> bool: ...
    @property
    def reason(self) -> str | None: ...
    def cancel(self, reason: str) -> None: ...
    def add_callback(self, callback: Callable[[str], None]) -> Callable[[], None]: ...

@contextmanager
def cancellation_scope(token: CancellationToken) -> Iterator[None]: ...

def current_cancellation_token() -> CancellationToken | None: ...

class StageRunner(Protocol):
    def cancel(self) -> None: ...

class ZephyrCoordinator:
    def abort_execution(self, execution_id: str, reason: str) -> None: ...

class ZephyrWorker:
    def cancel_execution(self, execution_id: str) -> None: ...
```

`CancellationToken.cancel()` is idempotent. Callback removal prevents cancellation after a completed operation.

## Testing

A Marin regression test will force a real local lease takeover. It will verify immediate token cancellation and no terminal write by the losing worker.

A Zephyr integration test will cancel a blocked subprocess execution. It will verify prompt return and successful work on the same shared pool afterward.

Coordinator tests will verify that one abort leaves a second execution active. Runner tests will verify child termination and callback races.

## Open Questions

- Is best-effort cancellation for `InlineRunner` sufficient, or should cooperative cancellation be a separate change?

Implemented in #8109.

Lease loss now cancels the active Fray job or Zephyr execution. The losing driver waits for the winning terminal result without writing a failure status or using a failure-budget attempt. Zephyr cancellation stops only the selected execution and keeps other shared-pool work active.

The full Marin package passed with 1,274 tests, 3 skips, and 5 expected failures. The Zephyr package passed 369 tests; two Iris shutdown timeouts passed on exact rerun. The independent peer review found no remaining unhandled issue after follow-up fixes.

issues.title: step_lock: a lost lease does not stop the running step

issues.author: mcwitt
issues.body:
🤖 *This description is the authoritative summary and is kept current. The comment thread below is the chronological investigation log, including hypotheses that were later refuted.*

## Summary

On an 8-rack GB200 training job (`experiments/grug/moe_hero_fsdp`, 128 nodes × 4 GPUs = **512
GPUs**, cluster `cw-us-east-08a`), a **single rank** hits a device-side
`CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION`. That rank's CUDA context is destroyed, it reaches JAX's shutdown
barrier alone, the barrier times out ~5 minutes later, and all 512 ranks abort.

Observed on **nine runs**, across **three `marin` commits** and at least six different physical
nodes, at steps ranging from **2 to 161**. It is not tied to a specific node, commit, or model
configuration.

This is now the binding constraint on the #7344 investigation: it censored **5 of the last 11**
eight-rack ablation runs, each time killing the gang before the run under test could reach a
verdict. A run killed by this fault says nothing about the configuration it was testing.

## The error

```
jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError: INTERNAL: Failed to retrieve branch_index value on stream 0x…:
  CUDA error: Could not synchronize CUDA stream:
  CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION: an illegal instruction was encountered
```

followed by hundreds of `cudaFreeAsync failed to free …: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION`, `Error
destroying CUDA event`, and an allocator stats dump as the poisoned context unwinds.

Two things this is not:

- **Not the fault site.** CUDA errors are asynchronous; `branch_index` retrieval is merely the first
  point at which JAX synchronizes and notices the context is already poisoned. The offending kernel
  ran earlier and has not been identified.
- **Not an allocator problem.** The failing call is a **free**, under no memory pressure — `InUse`
  55 GiB against a 138 GiB limit. The allocator is reporting that a CUDA call returned an
  illegal-instruction error; it is the messenger.

## Reproduction

Reproduces on **stock `main` with no modifications** — most recently verified at
[`121b71af6`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/121b71af645d9078f11b90f181568cdcf0551eaa)
(2026-08-06). `ctrl9` was a deliberate control on a pristine tree (`git status --porcelain` empty)
and faulted identically.

**Prerequisites:** access to the `marin` Iris cluster, 8 free GB200 racks on `cw-us-east-08a`, and
`WANDB_API_KEY` in the environment.

```bash
git checkout 121b71af6
RID=ii-repro-$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)

uv run --frozen iris --cluster=marin job run --no-wait --enable-extra-resources \
  --target-cluster cw-us-east-08a --priority production \
  --cpu 2 --memory 8GB --disk 32GB --timeout 21600 \
  --job-name "${RID}-coord" -e WANDB_API_KEY "$WANDB_API_KEY" \
  -- python -m experiments.grug.moe_hero_fsdp.launch \
     --run-id "$RID" --dp-racks 8 --num-steps 2000 --version dev --run
```

**What that runs.** 512 GPUs over 8 NVL72 racks, one process per node driving 4 GPUs. 48 layers,
hidden 6144, 128 experts top-4 plus 2 shared, 48 heads / 12 KV, head_dim 128, seq 4096 with 512
sliding window, `attention_implementation="gpu_fa4_cute"`, `moe_implementation="sonic_cute"`,
`expert_chunks=4`, MuonH, `offload_opt_state=True`, bf16 compute / fp32 params, mesh
`replica_axis_size=8` / `expert_axis_size=1`, batch 8192 × 4096 = 33.5M tokens/step, real
(SlimPajama-6B) data. Config: `experiments/grug/moe_hero_fsdp/heuristic.py` (`build_hero_configs`)
and `launch.py`.

**Recommended one-line change.** Stock `main` dispatches with `max_retries_failure=3,
max_task_failures=10`, so a fault triggers an automatic in-place restart from step 1 under the same
job ID — which both hides the failure and destroys the state you came to inspect. At the
`resources=config.resources` call site in `experiments/grug/moe_hero_fsdp/train.py`, set
`max_retries_failure=0` and `max_task_failures=0` (the latter needs plumbing through
`dispatch_grug_training_run` in `experiments/grug/dispatch.py`, which hardcodes 10).

**Expected outcome.** One of two failures, and you do not get to choose which — the same job
produces either this fault or the #7344 silent wedge. Historically roughly half and half. This
fault has appeared as early as step 2 and as late as step 161; a 200-step run has a good chance of
surfacing it, but the hazard estimate is unstable at nine events.

**Two practical notes**, both of which have cost hours here:

- `--target-cluster cw-us-east-08a` is **required**. Iris child jobs inherit the parent's region,
  so without it the GB200 request pins to wherever the coordinator landed and returns
  `unschedulable: no scaling group provides device gpu:gb200`.
- Retrieve the fault with `--since-ms` timestamp windows, **not** `--tail`. During the failure the
  128 tasks emit roughly 15,000 log lines/second, so the crash is pushed out of even a
  40,000-line tail within seconds.

## Fault coordinates

All UTC; first `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION` line of the attempt. Useful for correlating against
cluster-side Xid telemetry.

| Run | Date | Commit | Fault time | Task | Node | Step |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ras8` | 08-04 | `75d12bd05` | 06:50:24 | 80 | `s38vxs64` | ~23 |
| `ctrl9` | 08-04 | `75d12bd05` | 08:21:16 | 5 | `s6xvxs64` | ~89 |
| `norasA` | 08-04 | `75d12bd05` | 14:27:16 | 13 | not captured | ~85 |
| `oldbaseB` | 08-04 | `5e496b051` | 15:28:11 | 86 | rack 5, subnet `10.186.210.0/24` | 146 |
| `affin1` | 08-06 | `ae5c93e70` | 03:17:14 | 98 | not captured | 5 |
| `affin2` | 08-06 | `ae5c93e70` | ~05:25 | 104 | not captured | 17 |
| `n3full` | 08-06 | `ae5c93e70` | 06:14:42 | 9 (rank 36) | not captured | 76 |
| `nowatch` | 08-06 | `ae5c93e70` | 14:11:03 | 61 | not captured | 2 |
| `nowatch2` | 08-06 | `ae5c93e70` | 15:31:04 (abort) | not captured | not captured | ~161 |

An earlier version of this description reported a ~14× fault-rate difference between `75d12bd05`
and `5e496b051` (p ≈ 0.035 at four events). **That should not be relied on** — five further faults
have since occurred on a third commit, and the step range widened downward to 2, so the per-step
hazard fit that motivated the comparison no longer holds.

## Relationship to #7344

#7344 is a silent hang: all 512 ranks alive, `failures=0`, zero error output, no timeout ever
firing, sit-times measured up to 4.4 hours. This issue is loud, single-rank, and kills the gang in
~5 minutes. The stated discriminator has been "does a rank die?".

**That discriminator may track the reporting path rather than the fault.** The current leading
hypothesis is one underlying event with two presentations: the runtime notices and the rank dies
(**this issue**), or a channel resets while the process stays alive and that GPU silently stops
advancing its NCCL work (**#7344**).

Three observations fit that:

- An illegal instruction demonstrably *produces* a hang-like downstream state — an NCCL RAS
  snapshot during one of these failures showed a single rack three AllReduce calls behind with
  every rank alive and none marked dead.
- During a #7344 wedge, py-spy stacks are **identical** on lagging and non-lagging ranks (all in
  `absl::...FutexWaiter::WaitUntil` inside `xla_cuda_plugin.so`) — what you would expect if every
  rank were waiting on a device that will never finish.
- CoreWeave Grafana shows **Xid 13** (user application fault: illegal memory access or
  **instruction errors**) and **Xid 43** (GPU stopped processing, channel reset) on `s7vpxs64`
  during a window overlapping a #7344 wedge.

**The decisive check, and the highest-value outstanding item:** do the rows above show Xid 13 on
the faulting task's node, while #7344 wedges show Xid 43 inside the RAS-identified lagging unit? If
both, the issues collapse into one. The correlation set — six wedges and five faults with exact
timestamps, hostnames and lagging units — is in
[#7344 comment 5204902541](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7344#issuecomment-5204902541).
Currently blocked on Prometheus/Grafana read access: from inside the container Xid is unreachable
(`dmesg` needs `CAP_SYSLOG`, `/dev/kmsg` is absent, `dcgmi` is not in the image, NVML never exposes
Xid).

## Tried and ruled out

| Hypothesis | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Local diagnostic instrumentation | `ctrl9` was a pristine-tree control and faulted identically |
| NCCL RAS telemetry (#7951) | `norasA` ran with `NCCL_RAS_ENABLE=0` and still faulted |
| Checkpointing (#7929) | `ras8` faulted at step ~23, before any 30-minute checkpoint could exist |
| A single bad GPU or node | Faults on at least six different physical nodes |
| Toolchain / our build — **only partially** | `uv.lock` is identical across the commits that do and do not fault, and jax/jaxlib/NCCL/cuDNN/Triton are unchanged. **Not ruled out against the upstream NVIDIA container** — see the note below the table |
| Model or program change | `model.py` / `heuristic.py` unchanged across the suspect commit range; the compiled program is essentially identical |
| Fleet heterogeneity | All 205 GB200 nodes report identical kernel, OS, driver, GPU/NIC firmware and node image |
| Container image skew *within* a job | Pod specs pin a commit-tagged image; resolved digest uniform across all 210 GPU containers |
| `reference`-attention as a trigger | All five 08-06 faults were on the stock FA4 config (`gpu_fa4_cute` + `sonic_cute`) |
| `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` as an attribution tool | **Backfires** — it *suppresses* the fault (0 in 1185 steps vs 3 in 417), so it cannot localise the kernel |

**Do not confuse this with the other allocator errors in these threads.** Three distinct ones exist:

| error | attention | status |
|---|---|---|
| 145 GiB `cuMemAllocAsync` OUT_OF_MEMORY | `reference` only | retired — ablation artifact, see #7344 |
| `cudaFreeAsync` → `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION`, no memory pressure | **FA4 (stock)** | **this issue** |
| ~115 GiB `cuMemAllocAsync` OOM under `JAX_ENABLE_PGLE=0` | FA4 | compilation artifact of that ablation |

### What the NVIDIA-container result does and does not cover

**#7344 reproduces on `nvcr.io/nvidia/jax:26.07-py3`** — upstream jax, jaxlib, XLA, CUDA 13.3 and
NCCL 2.30.7 from the image, behind a hard provenance gate confirming `libnccl.so.2`,
`libcudart.so.13` and `libcuda.so.1` all resolve to image paths rather than to our venv or any
`nvidia-*` wheel. So **the wedge** is not attributable to our build of the toolchain.

**That result does not transfer to this issue.** Only two runs have ever used that image: a 1-rack
25-step smoke (image-swap validation, cannot wedge) and one 8-rack run that wedged after ~115 steps.
Neither hit `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION` — but ~115 steps of exposure, against a fault observed
anywhere from step 2 to step 161, is nowhere near enough to call a negative. While #7344 and #7956
are still treated as potentially distinct failures, evidence about one cannot be borrowed for the
other.

**Reproducing *this* fault on the NVIDIA container is therefore open, and valuable.** It is also
awkward: this fault appears on the stock FA4 hero config, whereas every container run so far has been
ladder rung 1 (`reference` + `scatter`), because CuTe pulls in `quack` -> `torch.cuda` -> `nvidia-*`
wheels whose lib dirs jax's plugin prepends, shadowing the image's own CUDA and NCCL and defeating
the point of the swap.

## Open hypotheses

1. **A GPU or driver-level fault not visible in node labels.** Uniform labels do not exclude an
   intermittent defect. The Xid correlation above would settle this and is the top priority.
2. **Something timing-sensitive rather than a bad kernel.** That the fault vanishes under
   `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` points this way. Explicit synchronisation boundaries around attention /
   MoE / loss / optimizer preserve kernel overlap and remain the more promising localisation route.
3. **Something in the task container image.** The image is tagged `1c7e3818c-recovery1`, and
   `1c7e3818c` **is not a commit in this repository**, so it is built from a source not tracked by
   the `marin` SHA or `uv.lock`. Against this: run `obs4` was clean after that image was already in
   service. Closing it needs the image's provenance from whoever owns it.

## Environment

Measured on-node, not inferred. Identical across all 205 GB200 nodes in the cluster:

```
kernel                  6.17.13-155-gdec5393c-coreweave-arm64
OS                      Ubuntu 24.04
NVIDIA driver           595.71.05
GPU firmware (all 4)    97.00.B9.00.99
Mellanox NIC fw (all 4) 28.47.2526
node image              2.49.0 / ofed-d30da48-n595-kver6.17-gdec5393c-bundle-arm64
CUDA driver API         13020        CUDA runtime  13000
NCCL                    2.28.9
```

Python dependencies, pinned in `uv.lock`:

```
jax / jaxlib        0.11.0      nvidia-nccl-cu13    2.28.9
jax-cuda13-plugin   0.11.0      nvidia-cudnn-cu13   9.19.0.56
jax-cuda13-pjrt     0.11.0      triton              3.6.0
```

Hardware: `gb200-4x` nodes (2× NVIDIA Grace Arm v9, 144 vCPU, 960 GB LPDDR5X, 4× Blackwell),
`multinode-nvlink-ib` topology, gang-scheduled.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 **Update: #7951 (NCCL RAS telemetry) is exonerated, and the suspect range may be a red herring.**

**Third reproduction, RAS fully disabled.** Ran unmodified `main` @ `75d12bd05` with `NCCL_RAS_ENABLE=0`, which disables both NCCL's RAS subsystem and the collector added in #7951:

| Run | Config | Faulting task |
|---|---|---|
| `ras8` | main + local instrumentation | 80 (`s38vxs64`) |
| `ctrl9` | main, unmodified | 5 (`s6xvxs64`) |
| `norasA` | main, unmodified, **`NCCL_RAS_ENABLE=0`** | 13 |

Identical `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION` at `branch_index` retrieval, a third distinct rank. So my leading hypothesis was wrong: **RAS polling is not the cause.**

**Checkpointing (#7929) is also not necessary.** `norasA` did save a checkpoint at 14:25:16 and faulted at 14:27:16, which looked suggestive — but `ras8` faulted ~12 minutes into training at step ~23, well before its first 30-minute checkpoint could exist. So a checkpoint write is not required to trigger it.

**The fault is not step-locked**: step ~23 in one run, step ~85 in another, varying ranks each time. Reliably triggered, nondeterministically located.

## Why the commit range now looks doubtful

Within `5e496b051..75d12bd05`:

- `model.py` and `heuristic.py` are **unchanged**
- `launch.py` changes are confined to checkpointing, telemetry, and the progress watchdog
- **`uv.lock` is unchanged** — no JAX, jaxlib, CUDA, NCCL, or Triton bump

So the compiled program and the entire Python/CUDA toolchain are identical between the last known-good tree and the failing one. It is not obvious that *any* of those 15 commits can produce a device-side illegal instruction.

That leaves a real possibility that the change is **not in this repository at all** — a node image, GPU driver, or firmware update on `cw-us-east-08a` between the clean runs (2026-08-03 ~16:00–04:00 UTC) and the failing ones (2026-08-04 ~06:30 onward) would fit every observation better than any commit here does.

**Test in flight:** re-running `5e496b051` — the tree that completed 200 steps cleanly twice yesterday — on today's cluster.

- **Clean** → the regression really is in the 15-commit range, and I will bisect it.
- **Faults** → the repo is not the cause; this is a cluster-side change, and bisecting would have burned hours chasing a commit that does not exist. That would also make this an infrastructure escalation rather than a code fix.

Will report the result here either way.
