issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
The Snowball long-loop prototype in PR 11120 (SFT, then async RLOO RL, then Micro210 eval, then archive) cannot yet run ablations from the 10/05 SFT cooldown checkpoint, and several of its stages would make an ablation campaign unreliable. This issue lists every problem found in a read-only review of PR 11120 at [`9e1c63cc9c`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop). Each item was re-checked from code, specs, storage listings and Iris state. Nothing was launched. Paths below are relative to `experiments/post_training/long_loop/`.

Notes, a per-claim verification table and the corrections it produced: [gist](https://gist.github.com/karansag/46431ff7905e2ece8234e7aee311861c).

## Starting checkpoint

1. **The launcher rejects SFT checkpoints it did not produce itself, so it cannot start from the 10/05 release.** The 10/05 weights are usable; only the loop's bookkeeping files are missing. The release is `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05` @ `ac60d940`: 4,750 SFT updates from base step 157000 to 161750, with the LR decayed to 0.1x over the last ~475 steps. It has the same base as the loop. [`verify_adopted_sft`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/adopted_sft.py#L23-L75) requires `selected.json`, a consumed config whose model block equals the loop recipe, a lineage JSON and a payload inventory. Only `metadata.json` and `manifest.json` exist for the native step-161750 checkpoint (GCS us-central2, about 540 GB). A verified HF copy already exists in the compute region: `s3://marin-rno2a/marin/models/grug-datakit-sft-262k-20261005-ac60d940-r1` (52 objects, 39 weight shards).
2. **The loop's own SFT stops before its cooldown.** [`specs/sft.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/sft.yaml#L100) stops at step 746 of a 4,750-step schedule ([L194](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/sft.yaml#L194)), and the decay covers only the final 475 steps ([L60-L82](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/sft.yaml#L60-L82)). The LR stays at 5e-5, and only 3 of 19 data-weight phases (0, 250, 500) run. The result is a truncated SFT on a 10/05-derived mix with reproduction substitutions ([`specs/sft-data.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/sft-data.yaml#L36-L40)), not a cooldown checkpoint. The full-geometry run `long-loop-full-2026.11.09.12` succeeded on 11-10 (32/32 tasks, about 21.1 h on 256 H100).

## Infrastructure

3. **Every stage after SFT is blocked.** For the full spec, RL and archive return four runtime-qualification blockers ([`run_spec.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/run_spec.py#L173-L187), [`specs/rl.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/rl.yaml#L293-L295), [`specs/agentic.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/agentic.yaml#L29-L30)). RL at 102,400 tokens with CP4 has not been qualified on a real SFT checkpoint.
4. **The pinned revision is stale.** [`specs/round1.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/round1.yaml#L2) pins `6e24f53e`, and [`__main__.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/__main__.py#L66-L75) refuses a local launch from any other revision.
5. **No stage retries or resumes.** Automatic retries and checkpoint resume are off in every recipe: [`sft.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/sft.yaml#L15-L16), [`sft.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/sft.py#L60) (forces `load_checkpoint` off), [`rl.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/rl.yaml#L42), [`evaluation.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/evaluation.yaml#L21), [`execution.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/execution.yaml#L72). A preemption mid-stage loses that stage. Finished stages are reused, and a finished SFT can be adopted. Issue 11162 describes the same retry setting killing eval drivers on the first Kueue eviction in another harness.
6. **No end-to-end timing.** The coordinator cap is 36 h ([`execution.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/execution.yaml#L75-L79)). The RL job timeout is 9 h ([`rl.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/rl.yaml#L285)) and the eval job timeout 24 h ([`evaluation.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/evaluation.yaml#L184)). The measured SFT took about 21.1 h, leaving about 14.9 h. Whether RL, eval and archive fit in that time is unmeasured.
7. **Arms alias each other's outputs.** A stage path is `{prefix}/{name}/{version}` with no config hash ([`lazy.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/lazy.py#L228-L238)). RL and eval take fixed manifest names ([`spec_pipeline.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/spec_pipeline.py#L158-L160)) and the report is fixed at `long-loop/report` ([`runtime_timing.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/runtime_timing.py#L111)). On changed config at an existing path, the runner logs a warning and serves the cached output ([`artifact.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/artifact.py#L380-L415)).
8. **Eval traces from every arm go to one place.** [`evaluation.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/evaluation.yaml#L93-L94) fixes `output_path` to `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/long-loop/traces/2026.11.09/eval` and `run_id` to `2026.11.09`, and [`evaluation.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/evaluation.py#L270-L279) does not rebind them. RL traces are rebound per run ([`rl.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/rl.py#L154-L169)).
9. **There is no eval-only or RL-resume entry point.** [`__main__.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/__main__.py#L58) offers `sft`, `rl` and `archive`. The only adoption point is after SFT ([`spec_pipeline.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/spec_pipeline.py#L84-L99)), so re-evaluating an RL checkpoint means re-running RL.
10. **RL keeps every checkpoint.** `ckpt_interval 1` with unlimited retention ([`rl.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/rl.yaml#L4), [L43](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/rl.yaml#L43), [L115](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/rl.yaml#L115)). [`archive_stage.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/archive_stage.py#L96-L110) skips cleanup when W&B or timing evidence is partial. A native 67B checkpoint per RL step accumulates on the shared rno2a quota.
11. **CPU helper stages request 8 H100 each.** The input check, export, eval-input prep and archive stages each declare one 8-H100 replica ([`execution.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/execution.yaml#L1-L64)), counted against the 256-H100 cap.
12. **One missing rollout blocks the report and archive.** The report raises unless every selected path has a verified rollout ([`runtime_timing.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/runtime_timing.py#L88-L97)), and Harbor trial retries are 0 ([`evaluation.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/evaluation.yaml#L118)). A verified zero score is accepted.
13. **End-to-end timing coverage is unproven.** Native SFT timing is recorded, and the report loads native journals ([`runtime_timing.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/runtime_timing.py#L52-L65)). Stage spans include queue time ([L23-L38](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/runtime_timing.py#L23-L38)). No real end-to-end report has shown complete coverage.
14. **Some admission audits exist only on one laptop.** Runtime dataset payloads have SHA256 checks ([`spec_pipeline.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/spec_pipeline.py#L40-L53)). The audit annotations in [`agentic.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/agentic.yaml#L15-L17) and [`exclusions.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/exclusions.yaml#L69-L101) point to `/Users/...` paths that nobody else can read.
15. **Inputs and compute are in different regions.** Data, tokenizer and caches are in `marin-us-east-02a`, the archive license is in `marin-us-east-08a`, and compute is pinned to `cw-rno2a` ([`execution.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/execution.yaml#L66-L73)).
16. **The Tau3 exclusion reason is only in code.** [`eval_runtime/profile.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/eval_runtime/profile.py#L52-L54) skips `tau3-pi` (issue 11083). The eval manifest lists 20 paths without Tau3 and without the reason ([`evaluation.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/evaluation.yaml#L245-L271)).

## Mini and micro evaluation

17. **No usable baseline.** The only result, `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/long-loop/merged-micro-report/2026.11.09.10-post1`, has one verified rollout per benchmark, no repeats and no per-path wall time. It shows the plumbing works, not a score.
18. **Micro210 cannot rank small ablation effects.** The full spec selects 200 tasks and 440 attempts ([`evaluation.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/evaluation.yaml#L245-L271)), about ±9.8 pp at p = 0.5. Resolving a 2 pp difference needs about 4,800 independent items per arm for a 95% interval, or about 9,800 for 80% power. Paired-item variance is unmeasured.
19. **Settings differ from the EvalDash records, so scores are not comparable.** The loop runs thinking on for every benchmark ([`evaluation.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/evaluation.yaml#L67-L68)), at T=0.6 and top_p 0.95, with the Pi agent and 65,536/16,384 limits. The EvalDash records for the A3 SFT arm run thinking off for HumanEval+, MBPP+, CRUXEval, MRCR, GSM8K, TriviaQA and IFBench. They use mini-swe-agent for SWE-bench and Terminus-2 for TBLite, TB2 and DS1000, and 32k/8k limits for BFCL, DS1000, TBLite and SWE-bench (MRCR: 4,096-token cap).
20. **TruthfulQA uses a different metric.** Micro210 scores a generated boxed letter 0/1. The policy reports probability-mass MC2.
21. **Six policy benchmarks are missing.** FinanceBench, PIQA, WinoGrande, BoolQ, SOTOPIA-hard and Tau3 are not in the loop's eval.
22. **Tool use is thinly measured.** The full spec selects 10 BFCL tasks (the plumbing report had 1). The audit computes only verified reward, response tokens and stop reasons ([`eval_runtime/audit_results.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/eval_runtime/audit_results.py#L15-L50)), with no tool-call or schema-success metric.
23. **Five of twenty plumbing rows hit the output cap.** CRUXEval, MBPP+, MRCR, TB2 and AIME24 stopped at 16,384 tokens ([`evaluation.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/evaluation.yaml#L8)).
24. **Eval context is shorter than RL context.** Eval runs at 65,536 tokens with CP 1 ([`evaluation.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/evaluation.yaml#L7)). RL trains at 102,400 with CP4 ([`rl.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/rl.yaml#L8)).
25. **Judge variance is unmeasured.** The MiniMax-M3 judge on 8 H100 took 997 s to start and held about 5 H100-h for the 20-row smoke, including queue. Repeat stability is unknown.
26. **Micro210 has no launch path on main.** PR 10817 closed without merging. The loop carries its own runtime in [`eval_runtime/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/eval_runtime), and issue 10933 tracks a main-branch launcher for any model.

Done when:
- The loop can start RL from a pinned, verified HF export, and a short RL smoke from the 10/05 release passes the RL qualification gate.
- RL, eval, report and trace paths are derived from the run, so two arms with different settings cannot share outputs, and changed config at an existing path fails instead of serving the cache.
- SFT and RL resume from their latest checkpoint after preemption, and RL checkpoint retention is bounded.
- An eval-only entry point exists for an existing RL checkpoint.
- The ablation eval set has a measured noise floor (repeats or paired items) and settings matching the EvalDash records, or a stated reason for each difference.
- One end-to-end run reports per-stage active and queue time against the 36 h target.

🤖
# Research

[PR #11120](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11120) remains a draft at the commit reviewed in this issue. Its downstream graph accepts a native SFT selection, exports that checkpoint, and then starts RL; the available 10/05 HF export cannot satisfy the native selection contract. The run also has fixed evaluation trace and report locations, while recipe drift at an existing artifact path only warns and serves the cached result.

**Relevant code**
- [`adopted_sft.py#L23-L75`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/adopted_sft.py#L23-L75) — native selection contract
- [`spec_pipeline.py#L84-L178`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/spec_pipeline.py#L84-L178) — SFT-to-RL binding
- [`__main__.py#L58-L75`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/__main__.py#L58-L75) — stage entry points and revision gate
- [`artifact.py#L380-L415`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/artifact.py#L380-L415) — advisory cache drift
- [`evaluation.yaml#L91-L94`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9e1c63cc9cf49a906637025123e9b784b250ead2/experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/evaluation.yaml#L91-L94) — fixed trace identity

# Proposed Fix

Sequence the work on PR #11120 or narrow PRs based on its branch; avoid a parallel implementation of the draft loop.

1. **Adopt the 10/05 export.** Add a distinct HF-source manifest pinned to the release revision, model and tokenizer metadata, and an exact shard inventory. Verify the small metadata and every shard’s presence and size before allocation, then bind the verified HF artifact directly to RL. Keep the native adoption path for loop-produced SFT; make its full recipe reach step 4,750 and check that the final 475 steps enter cooldown.
2. **Isolate every arm.** Derive the arm identity from the resolved spec, source checkpoint, and code revision; use it for RL, evaluation, report, archive, and trace paths and run IDs. Pin each step’s expected fingerprint so changed settings at an existing path fail before cache reuse. Test that two settings produce disjoint paths and that a reused path with changed settings is rejected. Update the stale revision pin when the code changes.
3. **Recover after preemption.** Resume SFT and RL from the latest committed checkpoint under the same arm identity; enable stage retries and keep a bounded number of RL checkpoints while preserving the selected final checkpoint for archive. Exercise interruption and resume with a short run, including evaluation retry behavior. Remove the 8-H100 allocation from CPU-only helper stages once their runtime requirements are verified.
4. **Evaluate an existing RL checkpoint.** Add an eval-only entry point with a pinned checkpoint and no RL rerun. Record benchmark-specific settings against the EvalDash policy, including thinking mode, agent, token limits, and TruthfulQA MC2; mark any unsupported or intentionally different path as non-comparable. Repeat or pair baseline items to estimate the noise floor, then choose ablation sample sizes for the intended effect size. Track tool-call validity, output-cap hits, and missing-rollout retries. Coordinate the generic launcher and Tau3 work with [#10933](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10933) and [#11083](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11083); coordinate eval preemption with [#11162](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11162).
5. **Qualify before a campaign.** Run a short 102,400-token CP4 RL smoke from the pinned 10/05 export and retain evidence for backward/optimizer steps, full-turn masks, checkpoint save and restore, and the qualification gate. Then run one complete arm and publish active and queue time by stage, total time against 36 hours, artifact identities, and checkpoint storage use. Keep the full campaign blocked until those measurements pass.

issues.author: forklady42
issues.body:
In forge run `full-s-20261108` (arm S), the validator discards an adversary finding when the replayed grade falls outside the finding's `expected` reward bounds. The adversary (glm-5.3) often fills `expected` with the reward the candidate deserves. Its instructions ask for the bounds that "reproduce the WRONG grader behavior". The replay then returns the wrong reward that the claim describes, the finding is marked `met: false`, and the round records no finding. Tasks are accepted with a demonstrated grader defect.

Example: [adversary trial, `d04.structure.periodicity--23`, round 0](https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/72938424-45b7-4d76-ba27-48acf51fc207/v/3/#/run/forge%3Afull-s-20261108%3Ad04.structure.periodicity/item/d04.structure.periodicity--23/trial/0/adversary/adversary%2F0/0)

Reproduce:
1. Open the trial above. The adversary submits a correct answer key that contains the true sentence "Oxygen's first electron affinity is exothermic, but its second electron affinity is strongly endothermic."
2. Its `grade` call returns reward 0.0. `negation_violation` in `grade.py` zeroes any sentence that has "is exothermic" and an element name, including sentences about the first electron affinity. The grader's own diagnostics show `raw: 1.0` before the penalty.
3. The adversary calls `report` with `expected: {"status": "graded", "reward_min": 0.85, "reward_max": 1.0}`. The claim text ends "observed: graded with reward 0.0".
4. The validator replays the candidate and gets 0.0. The attempt record has `forge_finding.met: false` and trial reward 0.0.
5. The round's calibration has `roles.adversary: {"passes": 0, "graded": 1}` and `findings: []`. The decision is `accept`, `in_band`.

Expected: a finding whose replay confirms the behavior described in its claim counts as a finding, and the round decision is `modify`. A finding whose replay disagrees with `expected` is reviewed before it is dropped.

Scope, from a random sample of 200 of the 1,750 capabilities with worked items in this run (read through the viewer's `api/run` and `api/attempt` endpoints):

- 3,011 adversary findings had a graded candidate. The validator counted 2,573 and dropped 438 (14.5%).
- In 232 dropped findings the grader scored below `expected` (claimed false reject). In 199 it scored above `expected` (claimed false accept).
- 184 of 984 accepted items (18.7%) have a dropped finding in their final validation round. 280 (28.5%) have one in some round.
- Of the 200 dropped final-round findings on accepted items, 68 claim a correct answer scored 0.3 or less and 86 claim a wrong answer scored 0.9 or more.
- 149 of the 200 capabilities have at least one dropped finding.

A dropped finding is an unreviewed claim. Some are contrived inputs that no honest solver would produce. The count of real defects in accepted tasks is unknown until the dropped findings are re-evaluated.

The same path drops findings whose replay ends in a grader crash or `infra_error`, including findings that report the crash. Example claim on `d13.air.gas_control--15`: an integer above float range raises `OverflowError` in `is_number()`.

Other examples from the sample, all on accepted items:

- `d17.treatment.adapt--8`: a note that continues warfarin unchanged at INR 6.5 scores 1.0 because "no doses are held" matches the hold-dose pattern. `expected` was 0.75.
- `d16.disease.mechanisms--21`: the grader raises `IndexError` on "S7, or the seventh step" and a blanket `except` returns 0.0. `expected` was 1.0.
- `d08.aerospace.aircraft_performance--15`: a memo with final endurance 2.10 h (correct value about 2.62 h) scores 1.0. `expected` was at most 0.6.

A search of `main` for the adversary prompt text found no match, so this issue has no code reference.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

The active TaskForge rewrite is in #11111 and #11112; its validator is not on `main` yet. `claim_result` treats `expected` as the *observed wrong grade*: when the first replay misses that band, it skips fresh-machine replay and sets `met=False`. `assess` then ignores a graded finding with `met=False` unless the grader failure was independently classified as an authored defect. A task with an in-band solver result can therefore be accepted without reviewing the adversary's claim.

**Relevant code**
- [`validate.py#L80-L87`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/0ab5aa39bdff9617217cdc0efc52f8e1af89e4f5/lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/stages/validate.py#L80-L87) — conditional fresh replay and `met`.
- [`rules.py#L92-L110`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/0ab5aa39bdff9617217cdc0efc52f8e1af89e4f5/lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/stages/rules.py#L92-L110) — review filters findings.
- [`adversary.py#L17-L49`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/0ab5aa39bdff9617217cdc0efc52f8e1af89e4f5/lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/harness/tools/adversary.py#L17-L49) — report schema and tool description.

# Proposed Fix

1. Land a follow-up on the active TaskForge stack. Make the report distinguish the grader's *observed* outcome from the adversary's *deserved* outcome, and preserve the claim, candidate, submitted bounds, replay grade, and adjudication in validation evidence. Clarify the report tool and prompt together.
2. Recheck a bound mismatch on a fresh verifier. Add a separate, model-assisted review of the task, candidate, claim, and replay diagnostics that returns `confirmed`, `refuted`, or `uncertain` with a reason; uncertain cases go to manual review. A confirmed defect requests `modify`, an uncertain claim blocks acceptance, and a refuted claim remains visible. Keep authored grader crashes on the `modify` path and infrastructure failures on the incomplete/retry path.
3. Add decision-level regressions for this issue's false reject, a false accept, an unsupported claim, a warm/fresh replay disagreement, a grader crash, and an infrastructure error. The false-reject test must show that a replay of 0.0 can still request `modify` when the candidate deserves high credit, even if the submitted bounds say 0.85–1.0.
4. After landing, re-adjudicate the dropped findings in `full-s-20261108`, starting with the issue's 200-capability sample. Report confirmed, refuted, and uncertain counts and the accepted items whose decisions change; manually inspect uncertain claims. The 438 dropped sample findings are unreviewed claims, not 438 established defects.

issues.author: forklady42
issues.body:
Forge validation counts a solver trial as solved only when its reward is exactly 1.0, unless the task's grader sets `reward.pass_above`. Most graders that award partial credit do not set it. A trial that scores 0.95 or 0.98 then counts as unsolved, and the solve-rate band (`min_solve_rate` 0.25, `max_solve_rate` 0.75, 3 trials) labels the task from that count.

Require the author to set `pass_above` explicitly whenever the grader can return a reward strictly between 0 and 1, so the pass line is a stated authoring decision for each task.

Evidence from forge run `full-s-20261108` (arm S), all 1,750 capabilities with worked items, 32,090 validation rounds and 96,270 solver trials, read through the viewer API:

- In 99.75% of rounds, `calibration.solver.solved` equals the number of trials with reward exactly 1.0. No round left a 1.0 uncounted.
- 79 rounds in 46 items counted a reward below 1.0 as solved. The grader was fetched for 45 of those items, and each one sets `pass_above` (values 0.5 to 0.96). The validator already honours the field.
- In a random sample of 297 items with at least one partial-credit solver reward, 4 graders set `pass_above`.
- 6.1% of solver trials scored in [0.9, 1.0) and counted as unsolved. 11.9% of rounds contain at least one such trial.
- With a pass line of 0.9 applied to every round, 3,322 rounds (10.4%) get a different band. Of 3,198 items accepted as `in_band`, 451 (14.1%) become `too_easy`. Of 850 rounds sent back as `too_hard`, 236 become `in_band` or `too_easy`; 174 abandoned items had such a round.

Examples:

- [`d04.structure.periodicity--4`](https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/72938424-45b7-4d76-ba27-48acf51fc207/v/3/#/run/forge%3Afull-s-20261108%3Ad04.structure.periodicity/item/d04.structure.periodicity--4): solver rewards 1.0, 1.0, 0.905. No `pass_above`. Solve rate 2/3, accepted as `in_band`.
- [`d10.5.3--9`](https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/72938424-45b7-4d76-ba27-48acf51fc207/v/3/#/run/forge%3Afull-s-20261108%3Ad10.5.3/item/d10.5.3--9): solver rewards 0.989, 1.0, 0.989. Solve rate 1/3, accepted as `in_band`.
- [`d07.circuits.devices--23`](https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/72938424-45b7-4d76-ba27-48acf51fc207/v/3/#/run/forge%3Afull-s-20261108%3Ad07.circuits.devices/item/d07.circuits.devices--23): grader sets `pass_above: 0.8`. Solver rewards 0.9, 0.9, 0.9 count as 3 of 3 solved.

The accepted-item counts use each item's accepting round and exclude 1,968 accepts that reverted to an earlier submission. 216 rounds were skipped because the ledger's graded trial count differed from the validator's.

Done when:
- A task whose grader can return a reward strictly between 0 and 1 fails the build or validation step when `reward.pass_above` is absent, with an error that names the missing field.
- The author instructions state that `pass_above` is required for partial-credit graders and describe what the value means.
- A grader that returns only 0 or 1 still builds without `pass_above`.
- The validator's solved count uses the declared `pass_above` for every partial-credit task, and a test covers a 0.95 reward on both sides of a declared threshold.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

TaskCompendium sets `GradeResult.passed` from `FileReward.pass_above`, but stdout and Verifyit graders can emit numeric rewards without a threshold. Forge's review rule treats an unset `passed` as solved only at full credit. The submission gate checks lowering, so it cannot reject a partial-credit grader without `pass_above`. This spans the support-library and Taskforge rewrite stack in [#11108](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11108) and [#11109](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11109); neither PR claims #11186.

**Relevant code**
- [TaskCompendium reward models](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/39a77695fc517b7a78ac6efdc8e261a2a54a4088/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/models.py#L472) — numeric sources and `FileReward.pass_above`
- [TaskCompendium grading](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/39a77695fc517b7a78ac6efdc8e261a2a54a4088/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/grading.py#L293) — sets `GradeResult.passed`
- [Forge submission gate](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/39a77695fc517b7a78ac6efdc8e261a2a54a4088/lib/forge/src/forge/wiring.py#L209) — accepts lowered drafts
- [Forge validation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/39a77695fc517b7a78ac6efdc8e261a2a54a4088/lib/forge/src/forge/stages/validate.py#L156) — gathers graded trials
- [Forge review rules](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/39a77695fc517b7a78ac6efdc8e261a2a54a4088/lib/forge/src/forge/stages/rules.py#L30) — full-credit fallback

# Proposed Fix

1. Give every numeric reward source a declared pass rule: `pass_above` for partial credit, or an explicit binary reward contract. Keep the existing exit-code reward binary. Extend the schema and grading runtime for stdout and Verifyit rewards; retain the existing file-reward threshold and its strict `reward > pass_above` meaning.
2. Reject any observed reward strictly between 0 and 1 under a binary contract. Return an author-facing invalid-task finding naming the missing `reward.pass_above` (or the equivalent Verifyit field) from both author grading and validation, before solve-rate placement. Arbitrary grader scripts cannot be proven binary at build time, so this runtime check is required even with a declaration.
3. State the contract and strict threshold semantics in the generated author instructions. Binary graders remain valid without `pass_above`.
4. Add TaskCompendium grading tests for numeric and binary sources, plus Forge tests that put a 0.95 reward on each side of declared thresholds and verify the solved count, band, and missing-threshold feedback. Land this on the rewrite stack once the author/validate stages have a merge target, with the TaskCompendium contract change first.

issues.title: [taskforge] Require pass_above when a forge grader gives partial credit

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Evaluate Marin Hero on variant effect prediction using unconditioned DNA likelihood, healthy-individual conditioning, and zero-/two-shot classification. The initial 100-variant autosomal missense pilot, two demonstrations, and a reserved 300-variant development validation panel are prepared. All 402 reference windows match independent GRCh38 queries; seven offline tests pass.

Execution is blocked on a live endpoint for the intended Hero SFT checkpoint. A November 6 probe established DNA token-likelihood access on an earlier service, but no dataset inference or model-quality results exist. The source, manifests, validation evidence, and remaining gates are linked below.

## Description

This experiment measures variant effect prediction (VEP) capability in the Marin Hero SFT model.
MarinDNA supplies the dataset and reference evaluation protocol; VEP-bench supplies the classification input representation.
The pilot supports prompt and scoring iteration before a frozen-method comparison on a fresh, larger development subset.

### Dataset and reference scoring protocol

Reuse the dataset and scoring conventions from the Mendelian evaluation in [Open-Athena/marin-dna](https://github.com/Open-Athena/marin-dna/tree/cd45a510f83209ec11aa9b17f42738dc9ee63853/snakemake/analysis/evals_v2) as the reference.

- Dataset: `marin-dna/evals_mendelian_traits`, revision `4aed58e50c5dea0b878a665007af2ef9e5108e9f`.
- Split: `train`, which is the project's development split.
- Positives: pathogenic SNVs from OMIM, HGMD, and Smedley et al. 2016, with allele frequency below 0.1%.
- Controls: gnomAD variants with allele frequency above 0.1%.
- Matching: one positive and nine controls per `match_group`, matched within consequence/chromosome strata using distance features.
- Standard likelihood score: compute `LLR = log P(alt) - log P(ref)` for each strand, average forward and reverse-complement LLRs, then negate the average so larger scores indicate predicted pathogenicity.
- Established reporting: per-consequence, global, and macro-average AUPRC, with match-group bootstrap uncertainty.

The DNA-model kernel uses a four-nucleotide softmax and single-base tokens.
Hero's general-vocabulary token likelihoods define a related but different scoring protocol; do not claim numerical parity with that kernel.

### Pilot sample

Use ten complete missense match groups: 100 variants comprising ten pathogenic positives and 90 matched controls.
The two few-shot demonstrations are additional development examples, separate from these 100 evaluation variants.
Use autosomes only (chromosomes 1–22) throughout demonstrations, pilot queries, sensitivity checks, and fresh development validation. Exclude chromosome X before constructing any sampling pools.

Before selecting rows:

1. Verify the dataset's missense consequence label and select only missense groups.
2. Check eligible group counts and preserve complete groups.
3. Select deterministically with a recorded seed, without using model scores.
4. Record variant IDs, genomic build and coordinates, reference/alternate alleles, consequence labels, group IDs, source revision, and sequence checksums.
5. Verify reference alleles against the genome and extract centered 255-base windows: 127 bases on either side of the SNV.
6. Prepare both forward and reverse-complement inputs, transforming allele and position descriptions consistently.

Use the same pilot variants for every approach.
Draw few-shot examples from a separate part of the development split, excluding pilot groups, duplicate variants, and overlapping windows.
Prefer chromosome-disjoint example/query pools where the available missense groups permit it; record the actual separation used.
Do not use the held-out test split for prompt selection or development evaluation.

### Approaches to compare

Let `L_c(s)` be the sum of log probabilities of the DNA tokens in sequence `s`, conditional on prefix `c`.
Exclude the prefix itself and any EOS probability from this score.
For reference/alternate contrasts, retain identical conditioning text and use summed likelihoods rather than means over variable numbers of BPE tokens.
Define token-boundary handling explicitly before execution.

#### Template conventions

The following templates define the proposed initial comparison.
The proposed initial serialization is plain text through `/v1/completions`, with no chat role wrappers or additional system message.
This makes the exact text explicit; using the model's native chat template for classification remains an open design choice before execution.
Model-required BOS handling must be recorded separately and kept consistent.

- Replace `{sequence}` with either the reference or alternate 255-base window, in separate requests.
- DNA is uppercase, on one line, with no spaces.
- Likelihood inputs have no trailing newline; classification FASTA records have a newline before their closing code fence.
- `{reference_sequence}` is the complete reference window for a classification query; its alternate allele is specified by the compact VCF row.
- `{ref_base}` and `{alt_base}` are the alleles in the displayed orientation.
- Position 128 is 1-based within the displayed 255-base window, including after reverse complementation.
- Braces denote substitution placeholders and are not sent literally.
- Newlines shown inside templates are literal.
- Outer four-backtick fences delimit the classification templates; the inner FASTA/VCF three-backtick fences are literal model input.
- VCF columns are separated by literal tabs; each record uses synthetic contig `sequence` and local coordinates.
- No gene name, genomic coordinate, consequence category, or true query label is included in the query text.

#### 1. Unprompted sequence likelihood

Exact input template, used once for the reference and once for the alternate:

```text
{sequence}
```

There is no text before the DNA and no trailing newline.
Score all DNA tokens, excluding any BOS or EOS target.
Score `L_empty(ref) - L_empty(alt)` on each strand and average.
This is the basic Hero VEP baseline.

#### 2. Healthy-individual prefix

Exact input template, used once for the reference and once for the alternate:

```text
The following sequence is from a healthy individual:
{sequence}
```

The prefix ends in exactly one newline after the colon.
There is no trailing newline after the DNA.
Score only the DNA continuation, excluding the sentence and its newline.
Verify that tokenization permits this scoring boundary; do not silently include a token spanning prefix text and DNA in the DNA-only score.

Score `L_healthy(ref) - L_healthy(alt)` on each strand and average.
The likelihood comparison has exactly two prefix conditions: no text prefix and this healthy-individual prefix.

#### 3. Direct classification

Use a reference FASTA plus a compact five-column VCF, following VEP-bench's input representation.
Keep one variant per query; matched controls can come from different loci and do not constitute edits to one shared reference.
The compact table is a prompt representation, not a full standards-compliant VCF file.

Exact query template:

````text
Classify variant V01 for Mendelian disease.
The FASTA contains a 255-base reference DNA sequence.
The compact VCF describes one substitution in that sequence.
POS is 1-based relative to the displayed sequence, not a genomic coordinate.
REF and ALT use the displayed sequence orientation.

Reference sequence:
```fasta
>sequence
{reference_sequence}
```

Variant:
```vcf
#CHROM	POS	ID	REF	ALT
sequence	128	V01	{ref_base}	{alt_base}
```

Which classification applies to variant V01?
A: pathogenic
B: benign
Respond with exactly one letter: A or B.

Answer:
````

The query ends immediately after `Answer:`, with no trailing space or newline.
Score these exact candidate continuations, each beginning with one ASCII space:

```json
[" A", " B"]
```

Verify that each continuation is exactly one token in the complete prompt context and record its token ID.
Do not assume this from the single-letter spelling or from isolated tokenization.
If the proposed continuations are not single tokens, revise and record the answer serialization before the pilot.
Do not append punctuation, a newline, or EOS to either scored candidate.

```text
S_primary = log P(" A" | query) - log P(" B" | query)
```

Higher scores mean greater predicted pathogenicity.
Obtain both candidate probabilities under the original, unrestricted model distribution, either by explicit candidate-token logprob access or teacher-forced scoring of each continuation.
Top-1 logprobs alone do not guarantee that both candidate probabilities are available.
Score only the candidate token; exclude all query tokens and do not sample an answer or substitute self-reported confidence.
Compute forward and reverse-complement scores separately and average them for the primary score.

##### Reversed-label sensitivity check

Repeat the same query with only the option mapping changed:

```text
A: benign
B: pathogenic
```

Orient the reversed-map score toward pathogenicity:

```text
S_reversed = log P(" B" | reversed_query) - log P(" A" | reversed_query)
S_mapping_average = (S_primary + S_reversed) / 2
```

Report the primary and reversed scores and their agreement; retain the mapping average as an additional summary, then average across strands consistently.
This check doubles classification prompt evaluations and helps assess letter/order preference; it does not guarantee that all prompt bias is removed.

##### Small input-format comparison

On a few pilot cases, compare the FASTA/VCF format with explicit reference and alternate sequences while keeping the same A/B mapping, candidate strings, and scoring rule.
For that comparison, replace the main query template's opening through the VCF block with this exact text, then retain its question, options, and `Answer:` ending:

```text
Classify variant V01 for Mendelian disease.
The reference and alternate sequences are each 255 bases long.
The mutation is at position 128 (1-based) in the displayed sequences.

Reference sequence: {reference_sequence}
Alternate sequence: {alternate_sequence}
Mutation V01: {ref_base}>{alt_base} at position 128
```

Insert exactly one blank line before the retained question.
This is an input-format check, not an additional likelihood-prefix condition.

#### 4. Few-shot classification

Use the same FASTA/VCF representation and A/B candidate continuations with exactly two labeled missense demonstrations.
The zero-example condition is the direct classification template above.

Exact two-example template:

````text
Classify single-nucleotide variants for Mendelian disease.
Each FASTA contains a 255-base reference DNA sequence.
Each compact VCF describes one substitution in its accompanying sequence.
POS is 1-based relative to that sequence, not a genomic coordinate.
REF and ALT use the displayed sequence orientation.
A: pathogenic
B: benign
Respond with exactly one letter: A or B.

Example 1:
```fasta
>sequence
{example_1_reference_sequence}
```
```vcf
#CHROM	POS	ID	REF	ALT
sequence	128	V01	{example_1_ref_base}	{example_1_alt_base}
```
Answer: {example_1_letter}

Example 2:
```fasta
>sequence
{example_2_reference_sequence}
```
```vcf
#CHROM	POS	ID	REF	ALT
sequence	128	V01	{example_2_ref_base}	{example_2_alt_base}
```
Answer: {example_2_letter}

Query:
```fasta
>sequence
{reference_sequence}
```
```vcf
#CHROM	POS	ID	REF	ALT
sequence	128	V01	{ref_base}	{alt_base}
```
Which classification applies to variant V01 in the query?
Answer:
````

Each example letter is exactly `A` or `B`, derived from its known label using the displayed mapping.
The repeated `sequence` and `V01` identifiers are local to each example or query, not shared genomic identifiers.
Use one pathogenic and one control variant, both missense, for a class-balanced two-shot demonstration set.
Use one fixed, seeded demonstration set and order for the initial pilot, shared across all 100 queries.
The instruction and option mapping appear once at the beginning.
The final query ends immediately after `Answer:`.
Score the same `" A"` and `" B"` continuations with the same scoring and tokenization checks as direct classification.
All demonstration tokens are conditioning context, not scored targets.

Keep demonstration selection independent of query labels and scores.
For the reversed-label check, swap the option mapping and every demonstration answer letter together; retain the same examples and order.
For reverse-complement inputs, reverse-complement both query and demonstration reference sequences and complement their REF/ALT alleles.
The centered position remains 128, and biological labels remain unchanged.
Additional demonstration sets or order permutations can be explored after the initial pilot.
Label these results as using supervision despite frozen model weights.

### Shared-prefix caching and tokenization

Rely on vLLM's automatic prefix caching when enabled and supported by the scoring request path; do not implement a separate client-side KV cache.
For a centered SNV, the reference and alternate share the left flank:

```text
reference = left flank + reference allele + right flank
alternate = left flank + alternate allele + right flank
```

The shared prefix's likelihood cancels in the reference/alternate difference.
Both the variant and downstream sequence must still be scored: identical downstream letters have different conditioning histories after the mutation.
Cache reuse operates on identical token prefixes, so a base-level mutation can also change the boundary of the reusable token prefix.

The distinction to verify is between normal next-token scoring and requesting log probabilities for tokens already in the prompt:

- **A/B classification:** prefer obtaining both candidate probabilities from the next-token distribution without asking for all prompt logprobs, if the endpoint supports it.
  Repeated few-shot demonstrations can then benefit from the server's normal prefix caching.
- **DNA likelihood:** the straightforward `echo`/prompt-logprob route requests scores throughout the input.
  The current vLLM V1 guide states that such requests bypass prefix-cache reads and recompute the prompt, even with prefix caching enabled.
  Verify the deployed build's behavior rather than assuming the shared half is reused.

Before the pilot, verify tokenization and scoring boundaries and check available cache metrics for the actual request path.
Use server-managed reuse where available; a correct uncached baseline is acceptable for this 100-variant pilot, with its runtime recorded.
Consider a supported selective-scoring interface only if necessary for subsequent scaling, and validate score parity before adoption.

### Execution and completion criteria

1. **Prepare inputs and scoring definitions.**
   Verify missense membership, freeze the 100-variant sample and two-demonstration manifests, and save exact prompt templates.
2. **Validate a few pairs.**
   Inspect sequence construction, token boundaries, score signs, both strands, and actual caching behavior; check parity if using a selective-scoring path.
3. **Run the small development pilot.**
   Apply all four approaches to the same subset with bounded concurrency, request limits, and a recorded endpoint-use budget.
   Confirm these execution limits before launch; this draft does not launch a sweep or provision compute.
4. **Inspect and iterate.**
   Save per-variant reference/alternate likelihoods, classification scores, strand disagreement, prompt sensitivity, errors, latency, and token/cache accounting.
   Inspect within-group pathogenic-versus-control ranking and representative failure cases.
   AUPRC on ten positives is exploratory; the pilot does not meet the existing evaluator's 30-group threshold for standard per-subset reporting.
5. **Freeze and validate more broadly.**
   Freeze templates, demonstrations, score formulas, and selection rules before evaluating a fresh, larger development subset.
   Use established consequence-stratified metrics and paired match-group resampling to compare methods where sample size supports it.

Preserve raw scoring outputs and request metadata so scores can be recomputed without rerunning inference.
Keep pilot tuning results distinct from the later frozen-method validation results.
Do not describe this pilot as clinical validation or as an official benchmark result.

### Open decisions

- Confirm the served checkpoint identity and availability. The final Mochi base checkpoint discussed in #11168 is different from the quick-SFT checkpoint used in the November 6 probe; changing checkpoints requires an explicit protocol decision.
- Validate the implemented plain-completion templates and contextual A/B tokenization on the live model before the pilot. A native chat-template comparison remains a possible later experiment.
- Measure whether the actual scoring requests benefit from automatic prefix caching; uncached scoring remains an acceptable correctness baseline.
- Confirm request count, concurrency, wall-time cap, and timing with endpoint users before launch.
- Freeze methods after pilot inspection and before scoring the reserved 300 variants. Longer-context experiments remain subsequent work.

The initial prompt bytes, demonstration split, and seed are now recorded in the research archive; they are no longer unspecified preparation tasks.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Determine whether Marin Hero ranks pathogenic missense variants above matched common controls using sequence likelihood alone, and whether healthy-individual conditioning or labeled demonstrations improve those rankings.
Compare all four approaches on the same 100 variants, preserving forward/reverse-complement scores and matched groups.
The pilot can expose scoring failures and prompt sensitivity; ten positive variants are insufficient for a reliable benchmark claim.

## Status

As of November 10, 2026, preparation is validated and model execution is blocked.

| Evidence | Result and scope |
| --- | --- |
| Pinned input selection | 493 eligible autosomal missense match groups; seed 11181 selects ten complete pilot groups (100 variants, ten positives), two chromosome-1 demonstrations, and 30 reserved validation groups (300 variants, 30 positives). Demonstrations and queries are chromosome-disjoint; pilot and validation windows do not overlap. [Manifest](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/4789fcaf2b1de205425524aea2832caf993ad8b6/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/selected-variants.json), [selection summary](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/4789fcaf2b1de205425524aea2832caf993ad8b6/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/preparation-result.json). |
| Sequence validation | Source/harness labels, central alleles, 255-base windows, reverse complements, and checksums passed. All 402 complete reference windows independently match Ensembl GRCh38. [Reference evidence](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/4789fcaf2b1de205425524aea2832caf993ad8b6/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/ensembl-reference.summary.json), [raw public responses](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/4789fcaf2b1de205425524aea2832caf993ad8b6/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/ensembl-reference.jsonl). |
| Implementation | Exact templates, bounded scoring requests, per-request replay evidence, complete-matrix aggregation, strand/mapping sensitivity, and native MarinDNA matched-group metrics are implemented in the research archive. Seven offline tests and lint pass. This does not establish live deployment compatibility. [Source and notebook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/4789fcaf2b1de205425524aea2832caf993ad8b6/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/notebook.md). |
| Metric verification | Synthetic 10- and 30-group fixtures verify AP=1 for perfect rankings, zero paired deltas for identical methods, and the 30-group standard-reporting threshold. These are software checks, not model scores. [Validation record](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/4789fcaf2b1de205425524aea2832caf993ad8b6/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/metrics-validation.json). |
| Dataset inference | Not run. No VEP rankings, classification results, measured cache reuse, or model-quality conclusion are available. |

### Historical endpoint feasibility check

On November 6, 2026, an authenticated Hero service returned HTTP 200 for `ACGTACGTACGTACGT` through `/v1/completions` with `echo: true`, `logprobs: 1`, and `max_tokens: 0`. All eight DNA tokens received finite log probabilities, summing to `-25.680376634001732`, conditional on BOS and excluding EOS. Usage reported one internal completion token although the returned text contained only the input. The scorer accepts this accounting behavior while checking that echoed token IDs exactly match the input.

This proves likelihood access on that service at that time. It does not prove current availability, correct variant rankings, or prefix-cache reuse.

### Current serving evidence

The original service subsequently returned “No endpoint”; the latest serving-registry query found no serving endpoints. Searches of public Slack discussions, indexed Discord history, and GitHub did not identify a usable replacement. This is a discovery result, not proof that no private or unannounced deployment exists. Exact service URLs, deployment identifiers, authentication instructions, and private discussion links remain outside this issue.

For the **final Mochi base checkpoint**, [#11168](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11168) reports that evaluation awaits a Hugging Face export and a compatible serving build; [#11127](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11127) tracks export, serving support, and parity work. Those issues explain that checkpoint's readiness, but do not establish the cause of the earlier quick-SFT service's removal. The two checkpoints must not be silently substituted.

### Remaining work and Loom feedback

[Loom's proposal](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11181#issuecomment-6778568972) is partially implemented: the logbook, pinned manifests, reference checks, scorer, and offline tests exist. The code currently lives on a Marin-derived research branch in `marin-logbooks`; the proposed reusable harness under `experiments/evals/` and its first Marin PR have not been created. The research archive index entry is also pending.

1. Restore or identify a live endpoint for the intended checkpoint, verify its identity, and agree on the request/concurrency/time budget. No new GPU deployment has been provisioned.
2. Validate a few pairs against the real tokenizer and serving protocol: BOS handling, DNA boundaries, both contextual A/B probabilities, score signs, strand behavior, latency, and cache behavior.
3. Run all four approaches on the same 100-variant manifest; inspect rankings, failures, prompt sensitivity, uncertainty, and request accounting. Ten-group AUPRC remains exploratory.
4. Freeze the protocol, then score the reserved 300-variant development panel using paired match-group resampling. Keep the held-out test split untouched.
5. Publish the resulting conclusion and reusable Marin harness PR, and complete the archive index. Keep the issue open until the experiment's evidence supports its conclusion.

## Links

- [Research notebook, source, and validation evidence](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/4789fcaf2b1de205425524aea2832caf993ad8b6/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/notebook.md).
- W&B Report: not created.
- Important updates: preparation and software validation complete; dataset inference blocked. See Status above.

- [Mendelian dataset at the pinned revision](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marin-dna/evals_mendelian_traits/tree/4aed58e50c5dea0b878a665007af2ef9e5108e9f)

- [Pinned evaluation configuration](https://github.com/Open-Athena/marin-dna/blob/cd45a510f83209ec11aa9b17f42738dc9ee63853/snakemake/analysis/evals_v2/config/config.yaml)
- [Shared-prefix scoring kernel](https://github.com/Open-Athena/marin-dna/blob/cd45a510f83209ec11aa9b17f42738dc9ee63853/snakemake/analysis/evals_v2/src/marin_dna_evals/model/scoring.py)
- [LLR harness and strand aggregation](https://github.com/Open-Athena/marin-dna/blob/cd45a510f83209ec11aa9b17f42738dc9ee63853/snakemake/analysis/evals_v2/src/marin_dna_evals/lm_eval/dna_vep_llr_eval.py)
- [Dataset descriptions](https://github.com/Open-Athena/marin-dna/blob/cd45a510f83209ec11aa9b17f42738dc9ee63853/dashboard/src/data/datasets.json.py)
- [vLLM automatic prefix caching](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/automatic_prefix_caching/)
- [vLLM V1 prompt-logprob behavior](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/usage/v1_guide/#prompt-logprobs-with-prefix-caching)
- [Newer selective prompt scoring documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/training/prompt_token_id_logprobs/)
- [VEP-bench FASTA/VCF prompt representation](https://github.com/Open-Athena/VEP-bench/blob/205df32032b9ff6be11bc387879e8bed578839aa/configs/tasks/sge/prompt.yaml)

## Decision Log

- Target the Marin Hero quick-SFT checkpoint used in the original feasibility probe; re-establish service availability and checkpoint identity before execution.
- Use 100 missense variants: ten complete match groups, with ten positives and 90 controls.
- Compare exactly two DNA-likelihood prefixes: no text prefix and the healthy-individual sentence.
- Use FASTA/VCF classification inputs with synthetic contig `sequence`, A/B answer likelihoods, and a reversed-label sensitivity check.
- Use only autosomes throughout. Reserve chromosome 1 for two separate missense demonstrations, one pathogenic and one control; query groups use other autosomes. Fix selection and demonstration order with seed 11181.
- Reserve 30 complete fresh development groups (300 variants) for validation after freezing the protocol. Exclude pilot overlaps and keep the held-out test split unused.
- Rely on server-managed prefix caching where supported; verify the scoring request path and allow an uncached pilot baseline.
- Keep service URLs, deployment identifiers, and access instructions outside the public issue.

## Conclusion

No conclusion about Marin Hero's VEP capability is supported yet. Input construction and local scoring/reporting checks are validated; the historical short probe establishes likelihood access only. The next evidence gate is live validation on the intended checkpoint, followed by the pilot and fresh development comparison.

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
Track biology evaluation coverage, tooling, and results for reference models and Snowball.

[Biology evaluations catalog](https://openathena.ai/bio-evals/) · [Catalog source](https://github.com/Open-Athena/bio-evals)

**Living summary — updated October 22, 2026.** Detailed evidence is linked from each result.

### Current results

| Model / benchmark | Result | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Snowball v0.1 Smartie Step14 / BixBench corrections v3 / Pi 1.3.0 | **19/205 (9.3%)**; all scored, only 48 nonempty submissions | [Result and reviewed trace audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6300963037) |
| Snowball v0.1 / BiomniBench-DA / Pi 0.87.0 / 60-minute protocol | **4.24/100**; 50/50 scored, 12/50 with any nonempty report (5/50 with both) | [EvalDash](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/20261022-165801-snowball-v01-biomnibench-da-60min-full-b3c4) · [Comparison and audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6349556649) |
| GLM-5.3 / BiomniBench-DA / Pi 0.87.0 / 60-minute protocol | **71.14/100**; 50/50 scored, 45/50 with both reports | [EvalDash](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/20261022-165801-glm-5.3-biomnibench-da-60min-full-b3c4) · [Comparison and audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6349556649) |
| GLM-5.3 / MMLU biology | **462/554**; 81.79% mean subject accuracy, 83.39% pooled | [Run and subject results](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/glm53-mmlu-biology-full-20260918-191647) (Marina access) |
| GLM-5.3 / BixBench CLI v1.5 / Terminus-2 | **101/187 graded (54.01%)**; 18/205 ungraded | [Baseline and limitations](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667) |
| GLM-5.3 / BixBench-Verified-50 / Terminus-2 | **42/49 graded (85.71%)**; 1/50 ungraded; saved-answer regrade | [Regrade and provenance](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/180#issuecomment-5766684283) |
| GLM-5.3 / BixBench-Verified-50 / Pi 0.87.0 | **39/46 graded (84.78%)**; 4/50 ungraded | [Run investigation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6086246928) |

Across benchmark rows, variants, agents, judges, budgets, and grading policies differ. The two BiomniBench-DA rows share the task/input preparation, Pi agent, rubric/judge and budget policy, with disclosed model-serving differences and reused early completions. BiomniBench-DA tasks with no nonempty report score zero; these scores are rubric-score means, not accuracy. Other GLM rows separately report ungraded outcomes.

### Current findings

Snowball’s BixBench failures are dominated by **156 missing answer files**, plus one empty submission. Traces show answers left in chat, simulated execution without real tool calls, repetition, and specific analysis mistakes. Compaction count showed little association with missing files. BFCL also had **55/123 missing submissions**; four inspected examples show related submission/tool-use failures beyond biology, without establishing one shared cause. No scores were changed.

The completed BiomniBench-DA comparison scores **Snowball 4.24/100 versus GLM-5.3 71.14/100**, with all 50 outcomes per model verified against native rewards, sealed archives and EvalDash rows. Snowball produced no nonempty report on 38/50 tasks; GLM did so on 5/50. All 38 selected Snowball cases ended normally within 24 minutes, so the separately confirmed Pi timeout leak cannot explain them. This supports a file-delivery/tool-use gap under these model-serving configurations; checkpoint versus tool/serving integration remains unresolved, and this does not establish a general biology knowledge deficit.

The 60-minute protocol retained 83 unaffected outcomes from the earlier 30-minute budget and reran deadline-affected tasks from scratch. It uses five disclosed input variants and a replacement MiniMax judge/signed rubric scorer, remains supplementary, and does not change the release aggregate. The continuation used the [Harbor timeout repair](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/3bc27cbcffad1d92ad5d9bd4c83cd3f36bf89372); an unresolved `/tokenize` HTTP 502 diagnostic affects interpretation of one GLM timeout. [Full comparison, launch-source references, audit and limitations](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6349556649).

[Selected HF traces](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples) show recurring simulated execution, chat-only answers, and repetitive output-limit failures across BiomniBench-DA, BixBench, and BFCL. BiomniBench also has wrong-path and rejected-write examples. These support general execution/submission problems without establishing a shared cause; [the comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6297505720) records the examples and differing Pi versions.

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 The five-question GLM-5.3 BixBench CLI pilot completed with an answer from every task. The original verifier scored three answers: one correct, two incorrect, and two unscored because structured JSON generation exhausted the judge's token limit. The incomplete original run retains no aggregate metric.

A separate, uniform regrade of the same five saved answers added an explicit JSON-schema instruction to the judge. It produced one correct and four incorrect results, with no JSON errors; the three previously valid grades stayed unchanged. This is a five-question integration pilot with a disclosed judge-prompt variation, not a full-benchmark accuracy estimate. The original answers, trajectories, and scores were preserved.

The format repair is in [Harbor commit `97037f79`](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/97037f793efaae22e22da5b89bc9604d2e40e800). It preserves the comparison prompt, Boolean schema, judge model, and 1,024-token cap. Lint and formatting passed. The branch has no PR yet; existing registry snapshots still require regenerated or explicitly patched tasks.

Error review:

- `bix-11-q2`: 88/249 fungal trees exceed the treeness threshold, giving 35.34%, versus the reference's 35%. The regrader rejected the difference. This is a likely precision-related false negative; no score has been changed. The pinned question specifies no rounding rule, and its archive contains no reference notebook.
- `bix-52-q2`: the agent used pooled CpGs / genome length. The [reference capsule](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-4dceea58-7d66-4576-bfc6-88c026d5b7a9.zip) groups only chromosomes containing retained CpGs (notebook cells 11 and 39). Averaging those 20 chromosome densities yields 1.1283e-7, inside the reference interval. The notebook confirms the chromosome selection; the mean was recomputed from the saved table.
- `bix-28-q1`: the final analysis substituted raw terminal branch lengths and species-level medians for the [PhyKIT long-branch statistic](https://jlsteenwyk.com/PhyKIT/reference/commands/long_branch_score.html). The reference p-value has not been independently reproduced; its archive also contains no reference notebook.
- `bix-6-q7`: the agent used a top-1% replicate intersection, then mistook its own intermediate enrichment CSV for supplied results. The [reference notebook](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-f4dcda89-678d-403d-b155-1483d0071765.zip), cells 28–30, instead takes the minimum replicate P-value, selects values below 0.05, maps RefSeq IDs to symbols, and runs Reactome enrichment against measured genes. It reports “cGMP effects” with raw P ≈ 0.000024 and adjusted P ≈ 0.0327. These are saved reference outputs, not a fresh rerun.
- `bix-18-q2`: the mean swarming area was correctly rounded to 82,000.

Six additional fixed judge diagnostics accepted `35.0%` as equivalent to `35%`, rejected `45%`, and classified one value inside and one outside the CpG reference interval correctly. The exact-percent and higher-precision examples returned provider server errors, so this check did not resolve the rounding concern. No tolerance or solver setting was retuned.

The [previously documented protocol](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5736346928) and explicit environment overrides were retained. All five pilot agents submitted within their original time limits, with no observed disk exhaustion. The full 205-question run remains pending a decision on numerical grading; original scores will remain intact.

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 Reviewed all 86 recorded incorrect answers and all 18 ungraded outcomes from the [completed BixBench CLI baseline](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667), using saved answers/trajectories and the archived reference notebooks where available. No solver or judge calls were rerun. The result remains **101/187 correct (54.01%), with 18/205 ungraded**.

Each incorrect answer has a primary review category:

| Category | Questions | Interpretation |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Observed analysis or protocol divergence | 54 | Identified differences in statistic, counting unit, filtering, cohort, model or enrichment workflow. Some choices are underspecified in the question; these are not all established scientific mistakes. |
| Answer precision or representation review | 11 | Submitted values may differ through rounding or units; this does not establish 11 false negatives. |
| Question or reference adjudication | 7 | Contradictory targets, unclear counting/aggregation, or unresolved reference-data provenance. |
| Numerical or pipeline mismatch unresolved | 14 | Insufficient evidence to isolate the cause without reconstructing more of the reference pipeline. |

The review ledger records a finding, confidence level, trace evidence and pinned reference capsule for each of the 104 nonpassing outcomes. Original trajectories remain in the existing evaluation archive; the detailed review ledger is retained with the private evaluation handoff. The categories above are follow-up queues, not a corrected accuracy estimate.

Concrete analysis findings:

- `bix-61-q1`: reported **4,818 discarded read pairs across two samples**. The MDR trimming log reconstructs the reference's **344,895 discarded individual reads** exactly: 334,988 forward-only survivors + 1,075 reverse-only survivors + 2 × 4,416 fully dropped pairs. Both the counting unit and sample scope changed.
- `bix-28-q4` and `bix-45-q5`: substituted a different statistic. The former used terminal-branch means grouped by species instead of per-tree long-branch scores; the latter used BUSCO score/cutoff instead of [PhyKIT relative composition variability](https://jlsteenwyk.com/PhyKIT/tutorials/pages/01-summarizing-information-content.html).
- `bix-16-q1/q3`: raw Chronos scores were used without the reference's sign reversal. `bix-20-q1/q3`: unclassified variants entered the denominator; the reference excludes them, giving 13/14 and 35/37. These differences are visible in the [essentiality reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-bda54b38-9b49-4009-aad6-d5f52675438a.zip), cell 34, and [variant reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-2ccdbe37-0a92-47b5-9bab-fa8a8c470799.zip), cell 18.
- RNA-seq failures repeatedly differed in count normalization, outlier exclusion, covariates, nominal versus adjusted p-values, enrichment gene lists and background. For example, the [JBX13 reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-1d54e4a7-8b0f-4224-bd31-efcfded0d46c.zip) removes three samples and models replicate, strain and medium; several answers retained all samples and omitted replicate. The [UBE2M reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-308d53bf-1513-4a09-913b-3a1112f94e7b.zip) removes KL3/WL3 before enrichment, unlike the `bix-53-q6` answer. Exact contributions were not isolated through reruns.
- `bix-10` / `bix-29` severity questions also expose a reference-definition caveat: the [reference preprocessing](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-fbe0e950-76f2-4eb7-a216-a2d377970922.zip), cell 17, aggregates all adverse events per participant, although questions call the endpoint COVID severity. COVID-specific/event-level alternatives therefore need protocol adjudication.

Grading and reference findings:

- `bix-19-q2` is a calculation-versus-submission example: the agent computed **Cohen's d = 0.216284**, independently matching [reference cell 30](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-8c64b1fa-fdcc-41e2-be8d-2f0c8d5faaa1.zip), but submitted approximately **0.22**. That final answer falls outside the target interval **0.215–0.217**. Other precision candidates include 35.34% versus 35% and 5.23 versus 5.2. The 11 cases are `4-q1/q5/q6`, `11-q1/q2/q5`, `19-q2`, `28-q6`, `38-q1/q3`, and `54-q5`, all with prefix `bix-`. Tiny nonzero p-values are not automatically equivalent to literal zero; `54-q5` also has a model-input difference alongside its ratio/fraction representation.
- `bix-53-q4` has a confirmed malformed target: the question requests a **pathway count**, but the [original ideal answer](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/BixBench.jsonl) is **4.25E-04**. [Reference cell 79](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-308d53bf-1513-4a09-913b-3a1112f94e7b.zip) explicitly counts **2** pathways. The submitted answer was **1**, so fixing the target would not automatically make it correct.
- `bix-31-q2` contradicts its stated analysis. The target interval **−0.45 to −0.35** conflicts with **abs(LFC)>0.5**. [Reference cells 32–38](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-b1dbace7-f6e9-42ec-81e1-bcc24161cc27.zip) show FAM138A at baseMean **0.483698**, unshrunk LFC **−0.383938**, and shrunk LFC **−0.060666**. The target matches the unshrunk, low-expression row despite instructions requiring shrinkage and baseMean>10. The agent answered `NA`.
- `bix-52-q1` has a reference-data bug: [reference cell 14](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-4dceea58-7d66-4576-bfc6-88c026d5b7a9.zip) downloads **JD_Chromosome_Length.csv** into **ZF_Chromosome_Length.csv**. The agent's **1.52** ratio is internally consistent with the supplied lengths and site counts; the provenance of the target **0.47–0.67** remains unresolved. `bix-52-q5` also counts repeated records instead of distinct sites, so this data caveat does not explain all CpG failures.
- The remaining four primary adjudication cases are `bix-8-q6` (260 unique genes versus 680 transcript records; [reference cell 21](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-48a6b469-9c9d-4bef-b5b4-f29b7d6fa046.zip) counts rows), `bix-38-q6` (median of paired ratios versus ratio of group medians), `bix-43-q4` (8/514 DE genes versus 8/49 pathway genes), and `bix-22-q6` (the origin of the 0.3–0.4 correlation target was not established). These require explicit definitions or reference reconstruction.
- `bix-54-q4` additionally has reversed target interval bounds, but its submitted p-value lies outside even the sorted interval. This metadata defect does not rescue that answer.

The [verifier](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/97037f793efaae22e22da5b89bc9604d2e40e800/adapters/bixbench/src/bixbench/task-template/tests/llm_judge.py) asks an LLM for binary equivalence. It has **no separate global numerical-tolerance rule**; some targets contain explicit intervals. The JSON-schema repair changes response format, not this comparison prompt. Before any rescoring, define a consistent precision/adjudication policy and preserve the present native grades as a separate baseline.

The 14 missing-answer traces show long model fits, repeated workbook inspection, unresolved analysis choices, and sensitivity checks after intermediate results existed. More time alone is not a demonstrated fix. The two exit-137 cases show killed statistical processes; excessive worker creation is a plausible contributor, but an OOM cause is unconfirmed. One gateway failure and `bix-10-q2`'s persistent judge 503 remain ungraded. The latter has a saved answer outside its target interval, but no manual grade was substituted.

Next: adjudicate the flagged question/reference and precision cases; document the intended analysis protocols; then select a small set of failures for any separately approved controlled rerun. Keep any revised scoring or solver results separate from this baseline. The existing verifier JSON-format PR follow-up remains open.

Reference links above use dataset revision `f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a`; notebook cell indices are zero-based. Several phylogenetic and genomic-pipeline capsules contain no reference notebook, which limits causal conclusions for the 14 unresolved cases.

🤖 Agent-runtime summary for the [completed 205-question BixBench CLI run](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667). Measured from each original Harbor trial’s `agent_execution.started_at` and `finished_at`; all 205 have both timestamps.

The median agent runtime was **5.6 minutes per question**. The middle 50% took **1.7–15.5 minutes**, and the 90th percentile was **37.3 minutes**.

| Questions | n | Median, min | 25th–75th percentile, min | 90th percentile, min | Mean, min |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| All attempted questions | 205 | 5.6 | 1.7–15.5 | 37.3 | 12.8 |
| Solver completed without interruption | 185 | 4.7 | 1.6–13.8 | 20.5 | 8.6 |
| Final grade: correct | 101 | 2.3 | 0.9–9.2 | 17.3 | 6.9 |
| Final grade: incorrect | 86 | 8.1 | 2.8–14.8 | 26.5 | 12.3 |

These are elapsed solving times, including model responses, command execution, waits and tool/network latency during the agent phase. They exclude separately timed sandbox setup, agent setup and grading. Quantiles use linear interpolation at `(n−1)×p`.

**17/205 tasks (8.3%) reached the configured 3,600-second agent cap**: 14 had no submitted answer and remained ungraded; 3 retained gradeable answers. The other three interrupted agents had two process-kill failures and one gateway failure. Capped times measure time spent before termination, not the uncensored time required to solve those tasks. Recorded capped durations were 3,600.0–3,602.3 seconds.

The median complete trial duration, including setup, grading and teardown, was **7.3 minutes**. The interval from the first trial start to the last trial finish was **3 h 28 min 48 s**.

The 185 uninterrupted solver completions include one answer whose judge still failed. Correct/incorrect rows use final saved-answer recovery grades and retain the three scored timeouts. Runtime differences between outcome groups are descriptive; task difficulty and workflow differences confound interpretation.

The complete launcher-to-export span was **3 h 36 min 11 s**, with a cap of **16 concurrent trials**. That batch span includes setup and final export; later saved-answer judge recovery is excluded. The [existing result](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667) remains 101/187 correct with 18 ungraded.

Per-question times, raw timestamps, source hashes and the summary calculation are retained in the private evaluation handoff. No new evaluation or grading calls were made.

No original reference notebook was available for this capsule. | Ask for a nonzero reference p-value with documented test options, or an explicit threshold/rounding instruction. Do not infer that every small p-value is equivalent to zero. |

Both the saved calculation and notebook give Cohen's d = 0.2162844172. | [bix-22-q6](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-34a4ea96-c800-4c11-959e-57cdc4932c52.zip) | 0.0504 → Between 0.3 and 0.4 inclusive | **Unresolved analysis specification**.
